title: Identifying DNA-binding proteins by combining support vector machine and PSSM distance transformation.
data_needed: benchmark of 1075 PDB chains (525 DNA-binding / 550 non) with sequences; independent PDB186 set; PSI-BLAST PSSMs vs NR
where: 1752-0509-9-S1-S10-S1.pdf (PDB IDs + sequences); PDB186 from Lou et al. 2014; NCBI nr
note: The supplement PDF lists the benchmark IDs and sequences. pdftotext recovered ~1044 headers against 1075 stated, so parse carefully or refetch by PDB ID. The PDB186 test set comes from another paper's supplement. PSSMs depend on today's much larger nr, which shifts the features.

title: Machine learning approach to predict protein phosphorylation sites by incorporating evolutionary information.
data_needed: Phospho.ELM 8.1 phosphosites with protein sequences (datasets A, A', A''), independent benchmark B; PSSM profiles
where: 1471-2105-11-273-S1.ZIP..S4.ZIP (A/A'/A''/B datasets as csv/txt/xls/ods: accession, phosphorylated positions, sequence)
note: All training and test sets, with sequences and site positions, are in the supplement (inspected). PSI-BLAST PSSMs must be regenerated against today's nr (drift). Phospho.ELM is still alive if needed.

title: YANA - a software tool for analyzing flux modes, gene-expression and enzyme activities.
data_needed: glutathione reductase system metabolic network (78 metabolites, 61 reactions) and example flux/expression scenarios
where: 1471-2105-6-135-S1.xls (sheets: metabolites, reactions with equations/reversibility, 134 elementary modes, flux distributions)
note: The full network definition and reference outputs (elementary modes, fluxes) are in the supplement (inspected). It is small and self-contained. Metatool or efmtool can stand in for EM calculation.

title: Integrated network reconstruction, visualization and analysis using YANAsquare.
data_needed: metabolic network definitions: reduced and extended phagosome phospholipid networks; genome-scale KEGG-derived networks of S. aureus, S. epidermidis, S. saprophyticus
where: 1471-2105-8-313-S1.pdf (Tables 1-15: metabolites, reaction equations, elementary modes for all five networks)
note: All network definitions are printed in the supplement PDF tables, which need extracting. KEGG is only needed to rebuild the networks.

title: PPInterFinder--a mining tool for extracting causal relations on human proteins from literature.
data_needed: PPI extraction evaluation corpora: human-protein subset of AIMed, HPRD50, an IntAct-derived set of 693 human PPI sentences, and curators' own 50-abstract sets from BioCreative 2012 + relation-keyword dictionary
where: supp_bas052_Supplementary_Data_bas052.zip: Supplementary_Data_1.xls (relation keyword dictionary, 88 roots), _2.xls (AIMed corpus text + per-sentence results), _3.xls (HPRD50 corpus + results), _4.xls (curator validation sets with PMIDs), _6.xls (IntAct 693-sentence dataset with labels), _7.xls (false positives); IntAct data-mining ftp (current only)
note: All four evaluation corpora (with gold labels and the system's per-sentence calls) and the keyword dictionary are in the 0.6 MB PMC zip, which is enough to reimplement and score the rule-based extractor. Still needed: external NLP pieces (protein NER, Stanford/other parsers) whose versions will differ. The tool site biomining-bu.in is gone.

title: Identification of properties important to protein aggregation using feature selection.
data_needed: AP1 aggregation peptide dataset (positives/negatives from literature, Swiss-Prot IDs) + AAindex-derived physicochemical features + SignalP 2.0 signal-peptide test set
where: 1471-2105-14-314-S2.doc (full AP1 dataset: peptide sequences + labels + source refs, 1.4 MB); 1471-2105-14-314-S1.doc and S3.doc (feature/AAindex lists); SignalP 2.0 set (DTU, see note)
note: The complete AP1 training/test dataset is in supplement S2 (checked: Swiss-Prot accession, peptide sequence, label, literature source). Features are AAindex records (public, listed in S1/S3). The only external piece is the SignalP 2.0 dataset (Nielsen 1999) for the extra test; CBS DTU moved to services.healthtech.dtu.dk and the old 2.0 set may need locating, but it is a widely circulated benchmark. Classifiers are standard (SVM-RFE, RF).

title: Supervised prediction of drug-target interactions using bipartite local models.
data_needed: Yamanishi 2008 gold-standard drug-target networks (enzyme, ion channel, GPCR, nuclear receptor) + KEGG chemical and sequence similarity matrices
where: http://web.kuicr.kyoto-u.ac.jp/supp/yoshi/drugtarget/ (bind_orfhsa_drug_*.txt; *_admat_dgc.txt; *_simmat_dc.txt; *_simmat_dg.txt)
note: Paper used exactly the Yamanishi 2008 ISMB datasets; that page still serves all four adjacency and similarity matrices (checked e_admat_dgc 0.6 MB, e_simmat_dg 8.3 MB). The paper's own cbio.ensmp.fr page is gone (archived only). This is the standard DTI benchmark, so many copies exist.

title: Predicting RNA-protein interactions using only sequence information.
data_needed: RPI2241 and RPI369 RNA-protein pair benchmarks from PRIDB/PDB chains (+ random negatives) and 5,166 mRNA-protein pairs from Hogan et al. 2008
where: 1471-2105-12-489-S2.TXT (2,241 positive pairs as PDB chain IDs); 1471-2105-12-489-S3.TXT (369 pairs); sequences from RCSB PDB
note: Supplements checked: tab-delimited protein_chain/RNA_chain PDB IDs (e.g. 1drz_A 1drz_B), 2,241 and 369 rows. Sequences must be pulled from PDB (some chains may be obsolete/remediated). Negatives were random pairings (re-generate; exact set not given). Third dataset (Hogan et al. 2008 PLoS Biol supplement) not checked; NPInter link in paper is gone (moved). Main benchmarks are fully reconstructable.

title: Application of support vector machine modeling for prediction of common diseases: the case of diabetes and pre-diabetes.
data_needed: NHANES 1999-2004 public-use files (demographics, questionnaire, exam, fasting glucose labs)
where: https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/ (e.g. https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/1999/DataFiles/DEMO.xpt)
note: NHANES 1999-2000, 2001-02, 2003-04 SAS XPT files still served by CDC (DEMO.xpt 11.5 MB checked). Case definitions and variable lists are in the paper (Table 1); training/test splits were random and not published. LibSVM is freely available; logistic baseline used SUDAAN (survey weights).

title: Bias in microRNA functional enrichment analysis.
data_needed: miRanda 3.3a genome-wide target predictions (miRBase 20 mature miRNAs x Ensembl 75 human/mouse 3'UTRs) + Ensembl 75 GO BP annotations + miRNA lists from 37 published studies (+ 4 rice studies with psRNATarget/agriGO); robustness checks with PITA v6, DIANA-microT-v4, starBase CLIP, DAVID BP_FAT
where: supp_btv023_supplementary_table_3.xls (miRNA lists + per-study miRanda/intersection/CLIP target lists); supp_btv023_supplementary_table_4.xls (rice miRNA + target lists); supp_btv023_supplementary_table_2.xls (study list); miRBase 20 (mirbase.org/download/PREVIOUS_RELEASES/20, alive); Ensembl 75 (ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-75, alive); agriGO v2 (alive)
note: The core inputs can be rebuilt exactly: miRBase release 20 mature.fa and Ensembl 75 3'UTRs/GO are archived, miRanda 3.3a is open source, and the PMC tables hold every published miRNA list plus the per-study target unions. The genome-wide predictions needed for the random-miRNA null must be regenerated (the project site sgjlab.org/empirical-go is gone, and microrna.org is 503). Secondary checks are weaker: PITA catalog v6 is not at its old Weizmann URL, starBase returns 403, and the DIANA-microT-v4 release is uncertain.

title: Comparative analysis of five protein-protein interaction corpora.
data_needed: five PPI corpora (AIMed, BioInfer, HPRD50, IEPA, LLL) converted to unified binary-interaction XML
where: https://github.com/metalrt/ppi-dataset (unified XML/CSV of all 5 corpora); original mars.cs.utu.fi/PPICorpora (DNS fails, archived)
note: The authors' converted corpora site is gone. A third-party GitHub mirror (checked via git) holds AIMed/BioInfer/HPRD50/IEPA/LLL in the Turku unified XML (~16 MB, with its own train/test split). This is a later version of the conversion, so counts may differ slightly from the 2008 tables. Both benchmark extraction methods must be reimplemented.

title: mGOASVM: Multi-label protein subcellular localization based on gene ontology and support vector machines.
data_needed: Virus-mPLoc (207 proteins, Swiss-Prot 57.9) and Plant-mPLoc (978 proteins, Swiss-Prot 55.3) benchmarks + GOA UniProt release of 08-Mar-2011 + novel-protein test set from Swiss-Prot 2011-12
where: http://www.csbio.sjtu.edu.cn/bioinf/virus-multi/Supp-A.doc; http://www.csbio.sjtu.edu.cn/bioinf/plant-multi/Supp-A.pdf; https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/GO/goa/old/UNIPROT/
note: Both benchmark files download (276 kB doc, 470 kB pdf; accessions + sequences, need parsing out of doc/pdf). The EBI GOA archive keeps numbered releases: gene_association.goa_uniprot.93.gz is dated 2011-03-07 (728 MB), matching the paper's 08-Mar-2011 GOA. The 175-protein novel test set is not listed; must be re-selected from UniProt by entry date (approximate).

title: Using distances between Top-n-gram and residue pairs for protein remote homology detection.
data_needed: SCOP 1.53 superfamily remote-homology benchmark (Liao & Noble; 4,352 Astral sequences, 54 families) + PSI-BLAST profiles against nr
where: https://noble.gs.washington.edu/proj/svm-pairwise/ (scop.1.53.1e-25.fasta; all_seq_fam_membership.txt)
note: Benchmark files checked (fasta 0.9 MB, membership table 0.5 MB). Profiles need PSI-BLAST against an nr database; the 2013-era nr is gone so profiles will drift slightly. Classic benchmark with many published comparators.

title: Geometric de-noising of protein-protein interaction networks.
data_needed: Yeast high-confidence PPI network of Collins et al. 2007 (PE-score set, 9,074 interactions) for testing + human BioGRID 2.0.35 physical PPI network (23,543 interactions/7,930 proteins) for application; validation against HPRD, BioGRID 2.0.50, GO, KEGG
where: BioGRID 2.0.35 and 2.0.50 (downloads.thebiogrid.org/BioGRID/Release-Archive/, alive); Collins et al. 2007 MCP supplement (doi:10.1074/mcp.M600381-MCP200, publisher site 403 to scripts); pcbi.1000454.s002-s008.doc (predictions and validation tables = results)
note: Both main input networks are obtainable. The exact BioGRID 2.0.35 and 2.0.50 releases are still in the BioGRID release archive. The Collins 2007 high-confidence yeast set comes from the MCP article supplement, which is behind Elsevier (403 to scripts) but widely mirrored. The PMC supplements hold outputs (251 predictions, validated pairs, BioGRID experiment-type list), which are useful for checking a rerun. The HPRD validation part cannot be redone officially (hprd.org is down). Small networks and an MDS-style embedding: a good target.

title: Reconstructing gene regulatory dynamics from high-dimensional single-cell snapshot data.
data_needed: simulated single-cell snapshot data from FFL and toggle-switch ODE models + Moignard et al. 2013 HSC single-cell qPCR (18 TFs, ~600 cells)
where: supp_btv257_Ocone_267_sup.pdf (model details); https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fncb2709/MediaObjects/41556_2013_BFncb2709_MOESM81_ESM.xlsx (Moignard 2013 Suppl. Table 3)
note: Simulation models and parameters are given in the paper and its PMC supplement. The real data was downloaded and checked: 620 cells x qPCR Ct values (Abl1, Eif2b1, Erg, Eto2, Fli1, Gata1, Gata2, ...), 213 kB. Code (inferenceSnapshot.zip) is gone; diffusion maps are available in destiny (R).

title: ProLoc-GO: utilizing informative Gene Ontology terms for sequence-based prediction of protein subcellular localization.
data_needed: SCL12 (Hum-PLoc: 919 train / 1,122 test human proteins) and SCL16 (Euk-OET-PLoc: 2,423 train / 1,727 test) + GOA from UniProt 45.0 (Jan 2007) + BLAST against Swiss-Prot
where: http://www.csbio.sjtu.edu.cn/bioinf/hum/learning_data.txt; http://www.csbio.sjtu.edu.cn/bioinf/hum/testing_data.txt; http://www.csbio.sjtu.edu.cn/bioinf/euk-oet/TrainingData.txt; http://www.csbio.sjtu.edu.cn/bioinf/euk-oet/TestingData.txt; https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/GO/goa/old/UNIPROT/
note: All four benchmark files download from Chou/Shen's SJTU mirror (0.5-1.3 MB each, accessions + sequences). Old GOA UniProt releases from 2007 are in the EBI archive (~200 MB each); old Swiss-Prot releases are on the UniProt FTP previous_releases. Small, well-defined benchmark.

title: Predicting zinc binding at the proteome level.
data_needed: 305/2369 zinc-binding PDB chains (PDB June 2005) with labels and 5-fold splits; non-metalloprotein chains; PSI-BLAST profiles vs nr; human RefSeq proteome
where: 1471-2105-8-39-S1.tgz (SVM_evaluation_data: CH/CHDE split and LOO files: PDB chain, residue, label); S3.TXT (human predictions); RCSB PDB; NCBI nr
note: The supplement lists every chain and residue with its label and cross-validation split. Sequences come from PDB SEQRES (still available). Profiles depend on today's nr. One cited RefSeq (XP_374396) is obsolete, which only affects the proteome scan.

title: L-GRAAL: Lagrangian graphlet-based network aligner.
data_needed: BioGRID v3.2.101 (June 2013) physical PPI networks of 8 organisms + protein sequences and GO annotations from Entrez Gene; NAPA synthetic networks (supplementary analysis)
where: https://downloads.thebiogrid.org/Download/BioGRID/Release-Archive/BIOGRID-3.2.101/BIOGRID-ORGANISM-3.2.101.tab2.zip; NCBI Entrez Gene; https://github.com/bjyoontamu/NAPAbench (NAPAbench 2 only)
note: The exact BioGRID release is still in the BioGRID archive (organism zip, 23.5 MB, checked). Node/edge counts per species are given in the paper for verification. Sequences and GO annotations are only available as current releases, so GO-based scores will drift. The original 2012 NAPA benchmark seems replaced by NAPAbench 2 in the GitHub repo. Supplement xls holds predicted interactions (outputs).

title: MicroTar: predicting microRNA targets from RNA duplexes.
data_needed: experimentally verified miRNA targets in C. elegans, D. melanogaster and mouse (TarBase-derived) + miRBase v9.0 miRNAs + RefSeq full mRNA sequences
where: 1471-2105-7-S5-S20-S1.xls (verified targets with TarBase IDs, gene IDs, versioned RefSeq accessions); NCBI RefSeq (NM_001027093 resolves); https://www.mirbase.org/download/
note: S1 (checked) lists each verified miRNA-target pair with NCBI GeneID and versioned RefSeq accessions, so the exact mRNA versions can be fetched from NCBI. miRBase's site now offers only current and releases 20-22 over HTTPS (v9.0 only via ftp, untestable here), but these classic miRNA sequences are essentially unchanged. Genome-wide prediction counts will drift with RefSeq.

title: A comparison of the functional modules identified from time course and static PPI network data.
data_needed: DIP S. cerevisiae PPI network (circa 2010 release) + yeast metabolic cycle expression time series (Tu et al. 2005, GSE3431, 9,335 probes x 36 time points) with periodic-transcript list + SGD GO associations
where: GEO GSE3431 (live; series matrix on ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo); DIP yeast download (dip.doe-mbi.ucla.edu/dip/Download.cgi?SM=7: TLS certificate error from here, registration needed, dossier lists it as alive); GO gene associations (geneontology.org, alive); 1471-2105-12-339-S1.RAR (36 TC-PIN network files = derived networks); 1471-2105-12-339-S2.RAR (GO enrichment result tables)
note: The expression input (GSE3431) is live and small. The PMC RAR files hold the 36 reconstructed time-course networks, which helps verify a reimplementation even if the DIP release differs. The exact DIP yeast release is not stated; DIP needs registration and showed a TLS error from this host, so expect drift. Periodic-gene list from Tu et al. 2005 (Science supplement). RAR format needs unrar to unpack.

title: An integrated strategy for prediction uncertainty analysis.
data_needed: JAK-STAT pathway ODE model + Swameye et al. 2003 time-course data (dataset 1: pEpoR, pSTAT, tSTAT)
where: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Data2Dynamics/d2d/master/arFramework3/Examples/Swameye_PNAS2003/Data/pnas_data_original.xls; Swameye 2003 PNAS; supp_bts088_pua_supplement_maj_rev.pdf
note: The Swameye data are not in the supplement but are in the Data2Dynamics example repository (checked, 21 kB) and the original PNAS paper. The model structure is in the paper and supplement. This is a widely reused benchmark.

title: A Bayesian approach to targeted experiment design.
data_needed: JAK2/STAT5 signalling model (Swameye et al. 2003) with the original Swameye 2003 time-course data (pEpoR, pSTAT5, total STAT5; 'dataset 1') + simulated experiments for design
where: Swameye 2003 data: Data2Dynamics repo (github.com/Data2Dynamics/d2d, arFramework3/Examples/Swameye_PNAS2003/Data/pnas_data_original.xls, reachable by git) and the PNAS 2003 supplement; supp_bts092_TED_supplement.pdf (MCMC details, model equations, priors); original URL webber.physik.uni-freiburg.de/~jeti/PNAS_Swameye_Data/ (no connection)
note: The only experimental input is the small, classic Swameye JAK-STAT dataset. Its original Freiburg URL is dead, but the same 'original' data file is in the Data2Dynamics example collection (and the PNAS SI). The model, priors and MCMC settings are in the paper and its 3.4 MB supplement. Everything else is simulation. Compute: MCMC sampling of an ODE model. An excellent target.

title: A combinational feature selection and ensemble neural network method for classification of gene expression data.
data_needed: 7 Kent Ridge cancer sets: Golub ALL-AML, Gordon lung, Singh prostate, Alizadeh DLBCL, Petricoin ovarian (proteomic), Alon colon, Armstrong MLL, with the repository's train/test splits
where: https://mldata-static.ml.tu-berlin.de/repository/tags/data/cancer/index.html (Kent Ridge copies); R datamicroarray (github ramhiser/datamicroarray: alon, golub, gordon, singh); sdmc.lit.org.sg (gone)
note: The original Kent Ridge site is dead, but static mirrors list all seven (lung, prostate, DLBCL, ovarian, colon, leukemia, MLL). Confirm the train/test splits match Table 1. These are classic, small datasets.

title: Fast gene ontology based clustering for microarray experiments.
data_needed: Skotheim et al. 2005 testicular germ cell tumour / embryonal carcinoma Agilent arrays + GO annotations (geneontology.org, 2008) + random GO term sets for the speed benchmark
where: GSE1818 (GEO, linked to PMID 15994931, 30 samples); http://www.geneontology.org (current annotations only)
note: The expression series is in GEO; sample names used (EC_0502, EC_0564, ...) are listed in the text for the 4 vs 10 comparison. GO annotations and ontology have changed since 2008 (dated GO releases are archived by the GO Consortium); the runtime benchmark (GO term sets of 50-1000) needs no specific data. Comparators SemSim/GOSim are old R packages.

title: Topology-function conservation in protein-protein interaction networks.
data_needed: BioGRID 3.2.106 (Nov 2013) physical PPI networks for S. cerevisiae and H. sapiens + NCBI gene2go GO annotations (Nov 2013) + GO OBO; graphlet orbit counts computed from the networks
where: BioGRID 3.2.106 (downloads.thebiogrid.org/BioGRID/Release-Archive/BIOGRID-3.2.106/, alive); GO release archive (release.geneontology.org, alive; dated GAF/OBO); NCBI gene2go (current only); supp_btv026_supplementary_Data_1.xlsx and supplementary_information.pdf (significant GO term/orbit results)
note: The exact BioGRID release is archived. NCBI gene2go is current-only, so use a Nov-2013 GO release-archive GAF; expect slight annotation drift. Supplements hold result tables for checking. The goCCA.zip code is gone. Needs graphlet-orbit counting (e.g., ORCA) plus CCA, which is moderate compute for the human network.

title: Integrating high dimensional bi-directional parsing models for gene mention tagging.
data_needed: BioCreative II gene mention (BC2GM) training and test corpora with gold standard and alternative annotations + HUGO approved symbols/aliases
where: https://sourceforge.net/projects/biocreative/files/biocreative2entitytagging/1.1/bc2geneMention.tar.gz/download; https://www.genenames.org (current HGNC only)
note: The BC2GM corpus with the official evaluation script is still on SourceForge (the BioCreative site itself returns 403 to this client). HGNC dictionary is only available as current release (minor drift). Mallet 0.4 is old but CRF features are fully described; a standard benchmark with many published baselines.

title: FastPros: screening of reaction knockout strategies for metabolic engineering.
data_needed: E. coli genome-scale metabolic model iAF1260 (Feist et al. 2007) with glucose minimal-medium constraints
where: https://bigg.ucsd.edu/static/models/iAF1260.xml (10 MB SBML); https://bigg.ucsd.edu/static/models/iAF1260.mat
note: The only input is iAF1260, still served by BiGG (checked). BiGG's current version may have minor curation changes vs. the 2007 model. The list of producible metabolites/knockouts (Suppl. Table S1) was on the unreachable Osaka site, but that is an output; the PMC docx supplement has methods details.

title: Filtering, FDR and power.
data_needed: simulated microarray-like data (Langaas et al. setup, 1,000 replicates) + Den Boer et al. 2009 childhood ALL Affymetrix dataset for the subsampling experiment
where: paper text (simulation design); GSE13425 (GEO, Den Boer et al. 2009, resolves); 1471-2105-11-450-S1.PDF (theory and figures)
note: Simulation parameters are fully given. The paper cites the leukemia data by reference only; GSE13425 (and companion GSE13351) are the Den Boer 2009 series in GEO - the exact sample subset (two subtypes with many samples) must be matched from the text. Mostly a statistics paper; very reproducible.

title: Local Geometry and Evolutionary Conservation of Protein Surfaces Reveal the Multiple Recognition Patches in Protein-Protein Interactions.
data_needed: Protein structures from Protein-Protein Docking Benchmark v4 (176 complexes) + Huang dataset of 62 complexes (Caffrey et al. 2004) + sequence homologs for evolutionary conservation (JET/PSI-BLAST against UniProt)
where: PPDBv4 (zlab.umassmed.edu/benchmark/benchmark4.tgz -> zlab.wenglab.org, alive, 34 MB); PDB (alive; dossier PDB/GenBank accessions resolve); Huang/Caffrey 2004 set (Protein Sci, PMC2286531); pcbi.1004580.s008-s014, s017-s019 (per-protein result tables listing PDB chains of both test sets)
note: Both benchmarks are standard and downloadable. The PMC supplements list per-protein results (by PDB chain) for each class, which pins down the exact test proteins and gives target numbers. Conservation scores need PSI-BLAST against a sequence database, and today's UniProt differs from 2015, so expect drift in TJET. The VORFFIP comparison uses published predictions. A good structural-bioinformatics target.

title: Biochemical Network Stochastic Simulator (BioNetS): software for stochastic modeling of biochemical networks.
data_needed: none beyond the example stochastic gene-expression / cell-division model whose reactions and rate constants are given in the paper
where: paper text (model reactions and parameters)
note: Simulator paper: results are simulations of a small transcriptional model (exact SSA vs. Langevin/hybrid, 2-D histograms, timing over 200 cell cycles). Inputs are fully specified; any Gillespie/hybrid implementation can reproduce the comparisons. Timing results are hardware-specific.

title: Statistical inference of chromosomal homology based on gene colinearity and applications to Arabidopsis and rice.
data_needed: Arabidopsis thaliana chromosome sequences and gene models (GenBank NC_003070-NC_003076, 2006 annotation) + O. sativa indica 93-11 genome (RiceGD) with BGF gene predictions; all-against-all BLASTP
where: NC_003070; NC_003071; NC_003074; NC_003075; NC_003076 (resolve); https://ftp.ensemblgenomes.ebi.ac.uk/pub/plants/current/fasta/oryza_indica/pep/ (ASM465v1 BGI indica proteins)
note: Version drift: the RefSeq Arabidopsis records now carry the Araport11-era annotation, not the 2006 TAIR gene order; the BGI 93-11 assembly (ASM465v1) and its BGI gene set are in Ensembl Plants, but RiceGD itself is gone and whether Ensembl's indica gene models equal the BGF set used is not confirmed. Supplements S1-S3 hold the colinear blocks found (outputs), useful for checking a reimplementation.

title: A k-mer scheme to predict piRNAs and characterize locust piRNAs.
data_needed: piRNAs from NONCODE v2.0 (rat, mouse, human) + NCBI GenBank fly/nematode piRNAs (gi ranges); random negatives; locust small-RNA deep sequencing (Wei et al. 2009, 603,607 reads)
where: http://www.noncode.org/datadownload/ncrna_NONCODE[v2.0].fasta.tar.gz; NCBI nuccore gi157361675-157362817 & gi222138290-222138841; GEO GSE12640 (locust small RNA)
note: The NONCODE v2.0 archive is still downloadable (checked). The locust data are in GEO GSE12640 (confirmed via E-utilities; the GEO web page itself shows a CAPTCHA). The negative set is randomly generated as described, so it is reproducible only in distribution.

title: APOLLO: a quality assessment service for single and multiple protein models.
data_needed: CASP8 (training) and CASP9 (test, 107 targets) server models + native structures
where: https://predictioncenter.org/download_area/CASP9/ (server_predictions ~1.2 GB, targets); https://predictioncenter.org/download_area/CASP8/; RCSB PDB
note: All models and targets are still on the CASP download area. The data are large but standard. The feature programs used (SPINE, SSpro, etc.) need old versions.

title: Prediction of piRNAs using transposon interaction and a support vector machine.
data_needed: 13,848 Drosophila piRNAs (GenBank gi157361675-157362817 + GEO GSE9138), NONCODE v3.0 ncRNAs (negatives; human/mouse/rat piRNAs), UCSC RepeatMasker transposons (fly, human, mouse, rat); Chilo suppressalis small RNA-seq
where: GEO GSE9138; http://www.noncode.org/datadownload/ncrna_NONCODE[v3.0].fasta.tar.gz (44 MB); UCSC hgdownload rmsk tracks (dm3/hg19/mm9/rn4); NCBI nuccore
note: The core training and cross-species data are all public (NONCODE v3.0 archive and GSE9138 checked). Genome builds are not stated, so use the 2013-era UCSC builds. The source of the rice stem borer small-RNA data is not given.

title: A method for probing the mutational landscape of amyloid structure.
data_needed: amyloid sequences (Abeta and Iowa mutant, HET-s and mutants, tau, alpha-synuclein, etc.) + PDB-derived statistical potentials; literature ssNMR chemical-shift/H-D exchange structure data for evaluation
where: UniProt sequences; RCSB PDB; supp_btr238_ODonnell_196_sup.pdf/.tex (method details and figures); literature/BMRB for validation
note: The inputs are sequences, and the potentials come from a non-redundant PDB set. The 'true' secondary structures used for scoring come from the published NMR papers, which have to be collected. The exact PDB set behind the potential is not given.

title: Enumerating metabolic pathways for the production of heterologous target chemicals in chassis organisms.
data_needed: metabolic hypergraph of KEGG reactions/compounds (c. 2011) with chassis (E. coli) native reactions; random sub-hypergraph samples for runtime tests
where: KEGG (http://www.genome.jp/kegg/ REST API, current release only); 1752-0509-6-10-S1.PDF ... S6.PDF (figures, examples)
note: Algorithm/complexity paper. KEGG is still freely queryable via REST, but the 2011 release used is not distributed (KEGG FTP is licensed) so the hypergraph will be larger today; runtime comparisons used random samples that are not published. Supplements hold figures, a worked example and the server description only.

title: A semi-supervised learning approach to predict synthetic genetic interactions by combining functional and topological properties of functional gene network.
data_needed: Tong et al. 2004 yeast SGA synthetic genetic interactions (gold standard) + BioGRID PPI (12,990 interactions) + protein complexes (Gavin/Krogan 2006) + 4 yeast time-course expression sets (Cho, heat shock, Chu sporulation, Spellman)
where: https://downloads.thebiogrid.org/BioGRID/Release-Archive/ (releases from 2.0.17); Tong 2004 Science supplement; Gavin 2006 / Krogan 2006 supplements; GEO / SGD for expression
note: Every source is a classic public dataset, and old BioGRID releases are archived. The exact BioGRID release and complex lists are not stated, so the 12,990-edge network must be matched by trial. Supplement DOC is methods only.

title: IntelliGO: a new vector-based semantic similarity measure including annotation origin.
data_needed: 13 yeast + 13 human KEGG pathways and 10 Pfam clans as gene-set benchmarks + GO/GOA annotations with evidence codes (2009-10) + CESSM reference dataset
where: KEGG REST (pathway IDs listed in paper); Pfam/InterPro clans; UniProt; https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/GO/goa/old/ (dated GOA releases); http://xldb.di.fc.ul.pt/tools/cessm/ (503)
note: Pathway and clan identifiers are given in the paper, but their gene memberships and the GO annotations have drifted; old GOA releases are archived at EBI. The CESSM online evaluation tool returned 503, so that comparison may not be repeatable. The AmiGO-based LCA queries must be recomputed locally.

title: Prediction of kinase-specific phosphorylation sites using conditional random fields.
data_needed: Phospho.ELM version 0707 kinase-specific phosphosites (positives) and non-annotated S/T/Y in the same proteins (negatives); subset with annotation date >2004 for comparison
where: http://phospho.elm.eu.org/dataset.html (current v9.0 under academic licence); supp_btn546_bioinf-2008-1096-File002.doc
note: Only Phospho.ELM 9.0 (2010) is downloadable today (free academic licence click-through), not v0707; because entries carry annotation dates, a 0707-like subset can be approximated by date filtering, and Table 1 gives per-kinase positive/negative counts to check against. CRF++ is still available. The CRPhos supplementary site is unreachable.

title: Learning transcriptional regulatory networks from high throughput gene expression data using continuous three-way mutual information.
data_needed: synthetic networks sampled from specified conditional models + Basso et al. 2005 human B-cell microarray compendium + MYC Target Gene Database for validation
where: paper text (synthetic model definitions); GSE2350 (Basso et al. 2005 B-cell data, GEO, resolves); MYC Target Gene Database (myccancergene.org now a parked lander; data via Zeller et al. 2003 Genome Biol, PMC)
note: Synthetic data is fully specified. The real expression input is the Basso 2005 B-cell compendium, which is in GEO as GSE2350 (same data used by ARACNe). The MYC target validation list was the online MYC Target Gene Database, whose site is gone, but that gene set is published in Zeller et al. 2003 (open access). 1471-2105-9-467-S1.pdf is supplementary figures/tables.

title: Detecting overlapping protein complexes based on a generative model with functional and topological properties.
data_needed: yeast PPI networks: Gavin 2006, Krogan 2006 (core/extended), Collins 2007, DIP, BioGRID; gold standards CYC2008 and SGD complexes; GO annotations
where: paper supplements of Gavin/Krogan/Collins; BioGRID release archive (alive); DIP (TLS failed here); CYC2008 in Pu et al. 2009 NAR supplement (PMC2647312; wodaklab.org 503); SGD (alive)
note: These are standard complex-detection benchmarks, but the DIP and BioGRID versions are not stated. The CYC2008 home site returns 503, but its paper supplement is in PMC. The supplements are only results tables.

title: Mojo Hand, a TALEN design tool for genome editing applications.
data_needed: NCBI Gene/Nucleotide records for a 35-gene test set + ~2000 random genes (feature statistics), REBASE enzyme list; zebrafish flt3 exon 1 for wet-lab test
where: NCBI E-utilities (eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, alive); REBASE (rebase.neb.com, alive)
note: The paper says the 35-gene test set is 'listed below', but the list is not in the article, and the ~2000 random genes behind Table 1 are not identified. NCBI records and REBASE are live but have changed since 2012 (annotation drift). Example gene IDs in the text (567858, 32619, 802118, 19091) and the flt3 target can be rerun. The in vivo TALEN activity is wet-lab work. Algorithm is simple string search, so this is cheap to reimplement, but Table 1 cannot be reproduced exactly.

title: Fast-Find: a novel computational approach to analyzing combinatorial motifs.
data_needed: Drosophila cDNA (BDGP DGC) and EST FASTA libraries as of ~2005, plus published RNA-binding-protein motifs
where: NCBI dbEST/GenBank (current); fruitfly.org na_cDNA.dros / na_EST.dros
note: The 2005 snapshots of the BDGP cDNA/EST FASTA files are not available: fruitfly.org returns 403, and NCBI's current Drosophila EST/cDNA sets are much larger. Motif definitions are in the paper. The alternative-polyadenylation candidate counts will drift with the newer data.

title: Content-rich biological network constructed by mining PubMed abstracts.
data_needed: 770 DIP protein-protein relationships (DIP IDs + gene pair names) + PubMed abstracts (up to 50 most recent per pair, as of 2004) + 6-database synonym dictionary (SwissProt, LocusLink, GDB, HUGO, OMIM, SGD)
where: 1471-2105-5-147-S1.bz2 (dipSummary.xls: 770 rows of DIP relation ID, PMID, per-cutoff calls); 1471-2105-5-147-S2.bz2 (26k files of original result HTML with retrieved sentences and PMIDs); 1471-2105-5-147-S5.bz2 (LTP query results); PubMed E-utilities (alive)
note: The test set and per-query outputs are in PMC. Gene pair names can be read from the S2 directory names, and the cited PMIDs can be refetched from PubMed (restrict by date to 2004). DIP itself is unreachable today (dip.doe-mbi.ucla.edu does not connect). The synonym dictionary is not provided, and LocusLink and GDB no longer exist. Precision was judged by hand. Recall can be approximated well.

title: Synchronous versus asynchronous modeling of gene regulatory networks.
data_needed: published Boolean network models: mammalian cell cycle, T-helper (Mendoza), dendritic cell (114 nodes), T-cell receptor (Klamt), plus a 1263-node network
where: original model papers; https://ginsim.github.io/ ; https://www.biomodels.org/ (SBML-qual)
note: The logic rules for T-helper, TCR and cell-cycle models are published and re-hosted (ginsim.org domain is now parked; GINsim moved to ginsim.github.io). Sources for the dendritic-cell and 1263-node 'Network 1' models are not identified in the text. Th1/Th2 validation needs only the T-helper model.

title: TACOA: taxonomic classification of environmental genomic fragments using a kernelized nearest neighbor approach.
data_needed: fragments simulated from 373 complete bacterial/archaeal genomes in SEED (March 2008) + NCBI taxonomy
where: NCBI RefSeq/GenBank complete genomes; NCBI Taxonomy; supplements S1-S9 (results-only PDFs)
note: The exact 373-genome list is not given, and the supplements are only performance plots. The genome set can be approximated with complete genomes released before March 2008, but the taxonomy has been revised since then. Fragments are simulated, so with a genome list the data are easy to regenerate.

title: TiSGeD: a database for tissue-specific genes.
data_needed: eight tissue microarray datasets (GNF BioGPS human/mouse/rat and GEO/ArrayExpress series, ~123k profiles over 107/67/30 tissues) + literature-curated tissue-specific genes
where: GNF/BioGPS GSE1133 etc. (GEO); ArrayExpress; bioinf.xmu.edu.cn/databases/TiSGeD (gone, archived)
note: The paper does not name the eight datasets. GNF atlases are still in GEO, but the selection must be guessed. The literature-curated gene list was only in the database, which is gone.

title: Towards the identification of protein complexes and functional modules by integrating PPI network and gene expression data.
data_needed: yeast PPI network from DIP (2009 release, 4,950 proteins / 21,788 interactions) + Tu et al. 2005 metabolic-cycle expression (36 samples) + 532 known complexes (NAR reference) + SGD GO annotations
where: GSE3431 (Tu et al. 2005, GEO, resolves); https://dip.doe-mbi.ucla.edu/dip/Download.cgi (TLS certificate fails from here; registration required); SGD GO annotations (current only)
note: Supplements (S1-S5) hold only the predicted complexes/modules (outputs). Expression data is in GEO. The specific DIP 2009 yeast release could not be verified (DIP server presents an invalid certificate); DIP historically offers dated releases after free registration. The 532-complex gold standard comes from a cited NAR paper (likely CYC2008-type set; not checked). GO annotations only as current release.

title: Inference of dynamical gene-regulatory networks based on time-resolved multi-stimuli multi-experiment data applying NetGenerator V2.0.
data_needed: Three simulated LTI benchmark GRNs (FCT 5 genes, LCT 4, NCT 7; six time points, Gaussian noise) + hMSC chondrogenesis Affymetrix HG-U133A time series (TGF-beta1 vs TGF-beta1+BMP2, 10 time points, 3 replicates) + prior knowledge from Pathway Studio ResNet and Transfac 2010 PWMs
where: 1752-0509-7-1-S3.csv (RSAT/Transfac binding-site hits used as prior knowledge, 8 rows); S1/S2/S4 PDFs (plots of measured and simulated time courses); NetGeneratorBundle.zip (biocontrol-jena.com, gone; Wayback capture exists, not checked)
note: The benchmark networks are synthetic, but their parameter matrices are given only as figures, and the noisy sample data were in the lost NetGeneratorBundle.zip (an archived copy may exist). The hMSC chondrogenesis microarrays (Organon/Radboud, Piek et al. lineage) have no GEO/ArrayExpress accession in the paper, and a GEO search found no match. Pathway Studio ResNet and Transfac 2010 are commercial. The measured time series can only be roughly digitized from the S4 plots.

title: Identification of chemogenomic features from drug-target interaction networks using interpretable classifiers.
data_needed: DrugBank human drug-target interactions as in Yamanishi 2011 (4,809 interactions, 1,862 drugs, 1,554 targets) + PubChem 881-bit substructure fingerprints of drugs + Pfam domains of targets (UniProt)
where: PubChem fingerprint spec (ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubchem/specifications/pubchem_fingerprints.txt, alive); Pfam/UniProt (alive); DrugBank (go.drugbank.com, login/licence, 403 to scripts, current release only); cbio.ensmp.fr/~yyamanishi/l1binary/ (redirects to lab homepage = gone; Wayback capture exists)
note: The exact 4,809-interaction gold standard and feature matrices were on the authors' page, which now redirects to the Mines ParisTech CBIO homepage (only an archived copy might hold them). There is no PMC supplement, and the journal supplement link is indeterminate. Fingerprints and Pfam domains can be recomputed. DrugBank needs an account and serves only current releases, so the circa-2010 set cannot be rebuilt exactly. L1-regularised linear models are easy to reimplement on any recent DrugBank snapshot.

title: Assimilating seizure dynamics.
data_needed: Dual intracellular recordings (membrane potential) of CA1 pyramidal cells and OLM interneurons during in vitro seizures (rat hippocampal slices, from Ziburkus et al. 2006) + fully specified two-compartment Hodgkin-Huxley/ion-concentration model
where: Model equations and parameters in the paper; MATLAB code said to be in ModelDB (now modeldb.science, alive; entry not located); pcbi.1000776.s001-s003.tif (estimated-variable plots only)
note: The model-only parts (UKF tracking of simulated data) are fully specified and need no external data. The experimental voltage traces were 'provided by Jokubas Ziburkus' and are not deposited anywhere stated in the paper. Supplements are figures of estimated variables. Assimilating real recordings would need different public patch-clamp data or a request to the authors.

title: HomoMINT: an inferred human network based on orthology mapping of protein interactions discovered in model organisms.
data_needed: MINT protein interactions from model organisms (snapshot 2005-04-30) + InParanoid orthology groups (2005 release) + Integr8 proteomes, mapped to the human proteome
where: 1471-2105-6-S4-S21-S1.zip (dump-homomint.txt, 10,993 inferred human interactions with source MINT IDs and model-organism UniProt pairs); 1471-2105-6-S4-S21-S2.zip (homomint-2005-04-30.xml, PSI-MI); InParanoid old versions v2.0-v8.0 (inparanoidb.sbc.su.se/download/, alive); MINT (mint.bio.uniroma2.it unreachable; data now in IntAct, current only)
note: The PMC supplement is the output network, but each row keeps provenance (source MINT interaction ID plus both model-organism UniProt IDs), so it can serve as a check set. The full 2005 MINT input (including interactions that failed to map) is not archived: MINT now lives inside IntAct as current data only. Old InParanoid releases (v2.0-v4.0, covering 2005) can still be downloaded. Integr8 is gone, but UniProt proteomes replace it.

title: Prediction and analysis of protein solubility using a novel scoring card method with dipeptide composition.
data_needed: Protein solubility datasets: Sd957 (authors' curated E. coli set), Sd726 (Chan et al. 2010), SOLproDB (17,408 sequences, Magnan 2009), SdPROSOII (Smialowski 2012); dipeptide composition only
where: SOLproDB: download.igb.uci.edu/SOLP.fa (alive, 4.7 MB, 17,408 sequences, checked); 1471-2105-13-S17-S3-S1/S2/S3.pdf (scoring matrices and run results = outputs); iclab.life.nctu.edu.tw/SCM/ (503; Wayback capture exists); PROSO II site mips.helmholtz-muenchen.de/prosoII (503)
note: Of the four benchmarks, only SOLproDB is confirmed downloadable (UCI IGB mirror, SOLP.fa). The authors' own Sd957, and the copies of Sd726 and SdPROSOII, were on the dead iclab SCM site (an archived capture may hold them). The supplements give the initial and optimised dipeptide scoring matrices, which help check a reimplementation. The method is simple (400 dipeptide scores + genetic algorithm), so the SOLproDB comparison can be redone now.

title: GeneTools--application for functional annotation and statistical hypothesis testing.
data_needed: Weekly local copies of annotation resources (UniGene, EntrezGene incl. GOA/MGD/RGD, GO, etc.) as of 2006 + user gene lists; the heart-failure (CAD/DCM) example is illustrative and has no data
where: 1471-2105-7-470-S1.pdf (statistical test derivations); GO archive releases and current EntrezGene/GOA (alive); UniGene (retired 2019, final dump only); genetools.no (gone; archived)
note: This is a tool and statistics paper. The main content (eGOn hypothesis tests for GO over-representation and list comparison) is fully described in the paper and S1, so it can be reimplemented on current GO/GOA data. The 2006 annotation snapshots and the heart-failure gene lists in the worked example are not provided, so example numbers cannot be matched.

title: Evaluating contributions of natural language parsers to protein-protein interaction extraction.
data_needed: AIMed PPI corpus (Bunescu & Mooney 2004) + GENIA Treebank (parser retraining) + Penn Treebank WSJ (original parser training); outputs of 8 parsers (KSDEP, MST, Charniak-Johnson, Bikel, Stanford, Sagae, ENJU, ENJU-GENIA)
where: AIMed: original UT Austin ftp unreachable; third-party copy in metalrt/ppi-dataset (git, alive: csv_output/AIMed-*.xml); GENIA Treebank: geniaproject.org redirects to a Google sign-in page and nactem.ac.uk/GENIA paths 404; Penn Treebank (LDC99T42, LDC licence, paid)
note: The evaluation corpus survives only through third-party redistributions. The original AIMed ftp is unreachable and the copy found is in Pyysalo-style unified XML, so the train/test fold split may differ. The GENIA Treebank download page could not be reached by script. The Penn Treebank is LDC-licensed and paid. Several parser links (Enju, pennconverter, Bikel, Berkeley) are gone. Rerunning modern versions of the parsers is possible, but exact f-scores will drift.

title: Overview of the gene ontology task at BioCreative IV.
data_needed: BC4GO corpus: 200 full-text PMC articles (100 train/50 dev/50 test) in BioC with curator-marked GO evidence passages and gene-GO annotations (+ team submissions for the evaluation)
where: BC4GO corpus via BioCreative (www.biocreative.org: HTTP 526 SSL error; biocreative.bioinformatics.udel.edu/resources/corpora/bc4go-corpus/: 403 to scripts); source articles are PMC open-access (alive); GO (alive)
note: The gold standard corpus is the key input, and it is officially distributed only from BioCreative sites that could not be reached by script today (biocreative.org has a broken certificate, and the UDel mirror returns 403). The article full texts can be rebuilt from PMC OA, but not the curator annotations. The teams' submissions, needed to reproduce the comparison tables, were never public. The hierarchical precision/recall/F metrics are fully defined.

title: Automatic concept recognition using the human phenotype ontology reference and test suite corpora.
data_needed: HPO gold standard corpus (228 OMIM-cited abstracts, 1,933 annotations) + 32-type test suites (2,164 HPO concepts) + HPO release of 2014
where: https://data.monarchinitiative.org/hpo/hpo_corpus.tar.gz (gold standard corpus: 229 text + 229 annotation files, 121 kB); http://bio-lark.org/hpo_res.html (gone, archived)
note: The gold standard corpus is still downloadable from the Monarch Initiative (checked; stand-off annotations by PMID). The test suites were only on bio-lark.org (gone) and possibly the OUP supplement (Cloudflare-blocked here). The 2014 HPO release must be taken from the HPO GitHub history. The compared tools (NCBO Annotator still live, OBO Annotator, Bio-LarK CR gone) limit exact reproduction. An improved GSC+ (Lobo et al. 2017) also exists.

title: Error correction of high-throughput sequencing datasets with non-uniform coverage.
data_needed: Illumina GAII reads from a single E. coli K-12 cell (MDA-amplified, Chitsaz et al. 2011 lane) + normal multi-cell E. coli lane ERX002508 (600x) + E. coli K-12 MG1655 reference
where: ERX002508 (ENA run ERR008613; submitted file ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/run/ERR008/ERR008613/200x100x100-081224_EAS20_0008_FC30TBBAAXX-6.tar.gz answers range GETs); NC_000913 reference
note: The multi-cell control dataset resolves in ENA (only the submitted tar.gz, no processed FASTQ). The single-cell lane that the main results use was distributed by UCSD (bix.ucsd.edu, no longer resolves) and the SPAdes mirror (cab.spbu.ru) gives 502 here; no SRA accession is cited and an ENA search did not find it. If it can be located (it was widely used as the 'E. coli single-cell lane 1' benchmark), the experiment is easy to rerun.

title: pSLIP: SVM based protein subcellular localization prediction using multiple physicochemical properties.
data_needed: Park & Kanehisa 2003 eukaryotic localization set (7,579 Swiss-Prot proteins, 12 classes, 5-fold splits) + Reinhardt & Hubbard 1998 eukaryotic set (independent test) + AAindex
where: http://web.kuicr.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~park/Seqdata/ (per-class 5-fold FASTA files, e.g. chlo1.dat); http://www.genome.jp/dbget/aaindex.html; Reinhardt-Hubbard set (SubLoc host www.bioinfo.tsinghua.edu.cn gone, ESLpred host connection reset)
note: Park & Kanehisa data is still served by Kyoto with the original 5-fold partition files (checked: FASTA with Swiss-Prot IDs). AAindex is alive. The Reinhardt & Hubbard independent test set could not be fetched from its usual hosts; copies probably circulate elsewhere (not verified). Cross-validation results (main table) can be reproduced now.

title: Performance of random forest when SNPs are in linkage disequilibrium.
data_needed: Simulated case-control SNP data under a range of genetic models with LD (r2 0-0.9) + TGen Alzheimer disease GWAS (Reiman et al. 2007; 861 cases/550 controls) with HapMap 2 CEU imputation around APOE
where: Simulation settings in the paper; TGen AD GWAS data (www.tgen.org/neurogenomics/data: 403 to scripts, cannot verify); HapMap 2 CEU (NCBI ftp archive, retired); rfld.html at Broad (404)
note: The core findings come from simulations whose genetic models are described in the text, so they can be regenerated without external data (exact replicates will differ, since no seeds or data are given). The real-data application uses the TGen AD GWAS, once a free download. The TGen site now blocks scripts (403), so availability is unknown, and the random 250/250 subsample and 103-SNP window cannot be recovered exactly. HapMap 2 is retired but archived.

title: Improving performance of mammalian microRNA target prediction.
data_needed: Positive training targets from miRecords (209 validated human miRNA-mRNA pairs, 2009) + negatives derived from 20 miRNA-transfection microarray experiments (GEO GSMs) + evaluation on pSILAC proteomics (Selbach et al. 2008) and miRNA transfection data
where: 1471-2105-11-476-S1.PDF (SI Table 4 lists the GEO GSM IDs for all 20 negative-set experiments); GEO GSM records (exist via E-utilities; web pages show a reCAPTCHA to scripts); miRecords (mirecords.biolead.org and c1.accurascience.com: 503, down); pSILAC site redirects to MDC lab page; compgenomics.utsa.edu/svmicro.html (gone; archived)
note: The negative set can be rebuilt exactly from the listed GEO samples (transfection arrays, 12/24 h). The 209 positive targets came from the 2009 miRecords snapshot. miRecords is offline, but its content was absorbed into miRTarBase and multiMiR, so the version will drift. Selbach 2008 pSILAC data are in the Nature supplement, not checked. UTR/site features also need 2009-era RefSeq UTRs.

title: Reconstruction of gene co-expression network from microarray data using local expression patterns.
data_needed: 13 DREAM3/DREAM4 in silico expression datasets + 7 real sets (yeast sporulation, Yeast KY, yeast cell cycle, GDS825, GDS958 subset, GDS3702 subset, Arabidopsis 'Thaliana')
where: DREAM via Synapse / GeneNetWeaver (gnw.sourceforge.net alive); GEO GDS825, GDS958, GDS3702; faculty.washington.edu/kayee/cluster/; cmgm.stanford.edu/pbrown/sporulation; homes.esat.kuleuven.be/~sistawww/bioi/thijs/Work/Clustering.html (unreachable)
note: The DREAM benchmarks (main AUPR/AUROC table) and 5 of the 7 real sets are public, so that part is ready now. The Arabidopsis set host does not answer, and the 4000/3000-gene subsets of GDS958/GDS3702 are not specified. The authors' resource page (Google Sites) is gone.

title: Using random forest for reliable classification and cost-sensitive learning for medical diagnosis.
data_needed: 8 UCI datasets (liver, pima, sonar, house votes, satellite, isolet [300-instance subset], soybean, covertype [500-instance subset]) + pediatric ALL expression data (Yeoh et al. 2002, 215/112 split) + UCI thyroid (7,200 records) + a Chinese-medicine chronic gastritis dataset
where: UCI ML Repository (archive.ics.uci.edu: thyroid, satellite, isolet, covertype pages alive); St Jude ALL data (stjuderesearch.org/data/ALL1: 403 to scripts; Yeoh 2002 data also redistributed, e.g., Bioconductor stjudem); chronic gastritis data (ref 23, no public source); 59.77.15.238/APBC_paper and penna.cn/cp-rf (unreachable)
note: Most benchmarks are standard UCI sets that are still downloadable. The isolet and covertype subsamples are not specified. Pima Indians Diabetes has been withdrawn from UCI (mirrors exist). The ALL data needs the St Jude page (blocks scripts) or a mirror. The chronic gastritis TCM dataset has no public source, so part II (cost-sensitive) is only half reproducible. The method (conformal prediction with RF) is simple to reimplement.

title: Kavosh: a new algorithm for finding network motifs.
data_needed: E. coli and S. cerevisiae transcription/metabolic networks plus a social and an electronic-circuit network from the Kashtan/Alon motif test collection
where: https://www.weizmann.ac.il/mcb/alon/download/collection-complex-networks (yeastinter_st.txt, s208/s420/s838_st.txt, prison/leader2 social networks); KEGG
note: The Alon lab collection is still downloadable (yeast transcription network, ISCAS circuits, social networks checked). The paper says it used 'up-to-date versions' of these networks and cites only database names for E. coli and yeast, so the exact edge lists are unknown. Results are mainly runtime/memory comparisons (vs. Mfinder, FANMOD, MAVisto), which are hardware-bound anyway.

title: Nonlinear dimension reduction and clustering by Minimum Curvilinearity unfold neuropathic pain and tissue embryological classes.
data_needed: 2DE CSF proteomic profiles of neuropathic pain patients (Pattini 2008; 23 samples x 2050 spots) + human tissue transcription-factor qRT-PCR atlas (Ravasi et al. 2010)
where: supp_btq376 (methods only); Ravasi et al. 2010 Cell supplement (TF expression)
note: The pain proteomics dataset was never deposited and is not in the supplement. The tissue TF expression data are published with Ravasi 2010. Only the second application is reproducible.

title: Alignment-free phylogeny of whole genomes using underlying subwords.
data_needed: 54 pandemic H1N1 2009 influenza genomes; 18 prokaryote genomes (accessions in Table 2); 5 Plasmodium genomes; reference trees (RDP 8.1 16S alignment, Martinsen 2008 Plasmodium taxonomy)
where: NCBI GenBank accessions in Table 2 (BA000002, AE000782, ...); NCBI Influenza Virus Resource; PlasmoDB/NCBI; rdp.cme.msu.edu (unreachable)
note: The prokaryote accessions are listed, so that benchmark is reproducible. The 54 influenza isolate IDs are not listed (the paper's page is gone), and the influenza reference tree source is unclear. Plasmodium assemblies have been updated since. RDP release 8.1 is unreachable.

title: SEQuel: improving the accuracy of genome assemblies.
data_needed: E. coli K-12 standard multi-cell Illumina reads (ERA000206), E. coli single-cell MDA reads (Chitsaz et al. 2011), single-cell SAR324 Deltaproteobacterium reads; reference NC_000913.2; assemblies from Velvet/Euler-SR
where: ERA000206 (ENA, resolves); NC_000913.2 (resolves); http://bix.ucsd.edu/singlecell/ (gone, archived)
note: The standard E. coli dataset and reference are public. The two single-cell datasets were distributed from bix.ucsd.edu, which is gone (Wayback capture listed, not downloadable here); no accessions are given for them. The single-cell E. coli lane may still be obtainable from SPAdes mirrors or SRA (not confirmed). Same single-cell data problem as Hammer (PMC3117386).

title: Frnakenstein: multiple target inverse RNA folding.
data_needed: RNA secondary-structure targets: 'Rfam data set' (29 structures from the first 30 Rfam families, as distributed by MODENA) + RNASTRAND-derived set (397 molecules/363 structures after redundancy and pseudoknot filtering) and its RNAfold-refolded version + multi-target design examples
where: RNA STRAND (rnasoft.ca/strand/download/RNA_STRAND_data.tar.gz, alive, 40 MB); Rfam archive (ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/Rfam/, alive incl. old releases); MODENA site rna.eit.hirosaki-u.ac.jp/modena (503)
note: RNA STRAND is still downloadable, so the 397-molecule set can be rebuilt with the stated filters (the exact membership after 80% similarity filtering may differ slightly). The 29-structure Rfam benchmark was taken from the MODENA website, which is down; it can be approximated from old Rfam seed structures, but the exact structures are not given. Multi-target examples are small and described in text. Uses ViennaRNA RNAfold (version drift affects results).

title: Cross-over between discrete and continuous protein structure space: insights into automatic classification and networks of protein structures.
data_needed: 2,890 domains with near-identical decomposition in SCOP and CATH (<40% identity), plus larger SCOP 5,041 and CATH 7,073 domain sets (2008-era releases); MAMMOTH structural alignments
where: https://scop.berkeley.edu/downloads/ (old SCOP/ASTRAL releases); http://download.cathdb.info/cath/releases/all-releases/ (CATH v2.0-v4.x archived, incl. v3_1_0); RCSB PDB
note: Old SCOP (via SCOPe) and CATH releases (v3.1.0 etc.) are archived, so the domain sets can be rebuilt, but the 2,890-domain consensus list itself was only on the ProtNet site (ub.cbm.uam.es, unreachable; Wayback capture listed) and the PMC supplements are figures. Matching criteria are described in Methods, so a close reconstruction is feasible.

title: Comparison study on statistical features of predicted secondary structures for protein structural class prediction: From content to position.
data_needed: four low-homology structural-class benchmarks: 25PDB (1673), 640, FC699 (858), 1189 (1092) + PSIPRED-predicted secondary structures
where: original dataset papers (Kurgan 2006/2008, Chen 2008, Wang&Yuan 2000) supplements; bioinfo.zstu.edu.cn/PSCP-PSSE (404)
note: The supplements are result tables only. The four benchmark sets are widely reused but were not located from here. PSIPRED output depends on version and database, so features will drift.

title: 'Double water exclusion': a hypothesis refining the O-ring theory for the hot spots at protein interfaces.
data_needed: 17,248 PDB X-ray complexes (March 2008, <2.5 A, >=2 chains >30 aa) for biclique mining + ASEdb alanine-scanning hot spots and HotSprint predictions for validation + Swiss-Prot residue frequencies
where: RCSB PDB (25 of 26 cited IDs live; 2hfm obsolete); https://asedb.org/ (now an unrelated site); HotSprint (interactome.ku.edu.tr, TLS certificate fails)
note: The structure set can be rebuilt from PDB with a release-date/resolution filter (several GB); a few entries are obsolete. ASEdb, the experimental hot-spot reference, is gone (domain now serves unrelated content), though its alanine-scanning data survive inside later benchmarks (e.g. SKEMPI, not checked). HotSprint not reachable with valid TLS.

title: EPMLR: sequence-based linear B-cell epitope prediction method using multiple linear regression.
data_needed: BEOD dataset derived from BEOracle (Wang et al. 2011; 4,405 epitopes and 8,467 experimentally verified non-epitopes from IEDB/BCIPEP/AntiJen) + SVMTriP dataset (4,925 epitopes + 4,925 non-epitopes from IEDB June 2012)
where: SVMTriP dataset (sysbio.unl.edu/SVMTriP/Download/posistiveset.tar.gz and negativeset.tar.gz, page alive); BEOracle data (sites.google.com/site/oracleclassifiers/, classic Google Site gone - redirects to sign-in); IEDB export (iedb.org, alive, current only); EPMLR site bioinfo.tsinghua.edu.cn (no connection)
note: The main BEOD benchmark is lost: it was built from the BEOracle release, which lived on a now-defunct classic Google Site, and the BEOracle paper's PMC supplement holds only methods text. The secondary SVMTriP comparison can be redone because SVMTriP still offers its positive and negative sets. IEDB could rebuild a similar set, but not the same one. Multiple linear regression on window features is trivial to reimplement.

title: ASH structure alignment package: sensitivity and selectivity in domain classification.
data_needed: 2911 sequence-unique CATH/SCOP domains (training) + Kolodny et al. 2005 test set (4,298,905 CATH domain pairs)
where: 1471-2105-8-116-S1.txt (2911 CATH domain IDs); S3.xls (per-query top hits); CATH archive https://download.cathdb.info/cath/releases/all-releases/ (v3.0/3.1); Kolodny test set (csb.stanford.edu DNS fails)
note: The training-set IDs are in the supplement, and matching old CATH releases are archived. The Kolodny 2005 test set host is gone, so the headline ROC (AUC .96) cannot be redone exactly. CATH domain IDs may need mapping to old releases.

title: Accuracy of phylogeny reconstruction methods combining overlapping gene data sets.
data_needed: Simulated gene alignments on species trees and taxon-coverage patterns taken from two real supermatrices: Gatesy et al. 2003 crocodile DNA data (25 taxa, 10 genes, 6,681 sites) and Driskell et al. 2004 green-plant data (69 taxa, 254 proteins)
where: Simulation design in the paper (Table 3; Figures 2-3 show coverage matrices and the crocodile species tree); Driskell 2004 matrices were on genome.cs.iastate.edu/CBL/ (gone) per the Science SOM; Gatesy 2003 crocodile alignments (TreeBASE, unreachable from here); supi software page cibiv.at (unreachable)
note: This is a simulation study, but it is anchored on two empirical datasets that give the species trees, branch lengths and gene-presence patterns. The crocodile setting can be largely rebuilt from Figure 2 (presence matrix and ML tree); the plant species tree and the 69x254 presence pattern need the Driskell matrices, whose CBL host is gone. The simulations themselves (Seq-Gen-style) need no other data.

title: Optimization algorithms for functional deimmunization of therapeutic proteins.
data_needed: therapeutic-protein sequences/structures (e.g. staphylokinase 2SAK, erythropoietin 1EER) + ProPred/TEPITOPE MHC-II pocket-profile matrices + FoldX for stability (DDG)
where: PDB 2SAK, 1EER (resolve); ProPred/TEPITOPE pocket-profile matrices (originally propred host, now via IEDB/other mirrors); FoldX (foldxsuite.crg.eu, academic licence); 1471-2105-11-180-S1.PDF (additional variants, output)
note: Optimization-method paper: inputs are a handful of named proteins (in PDB) plus the TEPITOPE pocket-profile weight matrices, which are small and still circulate (ProPred/IEDB), and FoldX for DDG (licensed, not free). No single dataset underlies the main results; the supplement lists the designed variants. Reproducible if the TEPITOPE matrices are located.

title: Statistical resolution of ambiguous HLA typing data.
data_needed: Four-digit and ambiguous HLA-A/B/C typing data: (1) private Carrington-lab disease cohort/control data (4 populations), (2) public dbMHC population datasets (Irish n=1000, North American Asian/European/Black/Hispanic/Amerindian) incl. 4-locus data
where: dbMHC Final Archive (ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/mhc/mhc/Final Archive/IHWG/Anthropology/Anthropology.csv etc., alive); Carrington-lab cohort data (private, not deposited); microsoft.com/science tool page (gone)
note: The main training/evaluation data are private HIV and disease cohorts typed in Mary Carrington's lab, so the headline numbers cannot be reproduced. The public dbMHC data used for the population-augmented and four-locus experiments survive in NCBI's dbMHC Final Archive (IHWG anthropology tables), though matching the exact population subsets used needs care. The EM/softmax model is fully described.

title: Automatic medical encoding with SNOMED categories.
data_needed: Cystic Fibrosis (CF) test collection (1,239 MEDLINE citations with MeSH; 239 tuning/1000 test) + SNOMED CT terminology + UMLS 2006 SNOMED-MeSH mapping
where: CF collection (people.ischool.berkeley.edu/~hearst/irbook/cfc.html, alive, ~1.5 MB); UMLS 2006AA/2006AB archives (nlm.nih.gov UMLS archives page lists them; UMLS licence required); SNOMED CT (licence via UMLS/affiliate); eagl.unige.ch/SNOCat (unreachable)
note: The evaluation corpus is a classic IR collection, still freely downloadable. SNOMED CT and the 2006 UMLS MeSH-SNOMED mapping need a (free) UMLS licence; NLM lists 2006 releases in its archive, but access was not tested. The 239/1000 tuning/test split is not given, and the 'dozen MEDLINE abstracts' qualitative study is not reproducible.

title: JLIN: a java based linkage disequilibrium plotter.
data_needed: User-supplied SNP genotype data; the paper's only example is an unnamed 6-SNP single-gene dataset
where: none (no supplement; project page genepi.org.au/projects/jlin is gone)
note: This is a visualization tool paper with no benchmark dataset; Figure 1 uses six anonymous SNPs (SNP1-SNP6). There are no numeric results to reproduce, only plotting of D', r2 and empirical p-values. A reimplementation can be checked against any public genotype panel (e.g., 1000 Genomes or HapMap) and other LD tools such as Haploview, so missing data matters little.

title: Structurama: bayesian inference of population structure.
data_needed: User-supplied multilocus allele data; the paper is a short software note with no named dataset
where: structurama.org (unreachable; archived)
note: This is a short application note for a Bayesian (Dirichlet-process) population-structure program with no benchmark data described in the text. Any public multilocus genotype dataset, or data simulated under a known structure, can test a reimplementation. Nothing paper-specific has to be recovered.

title: CGHPRO -- a comprehensive data analysis tool for array CGH.
data_needed: In-house array CGH data: male vs female co-hybridization on a 14,000-clone BAC array (Sanger 1 Mb set + additional clones) + artificially generated dataset for the comparative analysis + UCSC clone mapping
where: molgen.mpg.de CGHPRO page (gone; archived); BACPAC clone info (bacpac.chori.org, moved)
note: This is a software paper whose demo data were never deposited. The male/female BAC hybridization and the artificial comparative dataset are not in GEO or any supplement (there is none). Any public aCGH dataset (e.g., BAC arrays in GEO) or simulated log2 ratios can stand in. Little quantitative output needs to be matched.

title: MetaMQAP: a meta-server for the quality assessment of protein models.
data_needed: CASP5/CASP6 template-based models (training) and CASP7 server models (test) with native PDB structures; scores from 8 third-party MQAPs
where: https://predictioncenter.org/download_area/CASP5/; https://predictioncenter.org/download_area/CASP6/; https://predictioncenter.org/download_area/CASP7/; RCSB PDB
note: CASP5-7 model archives (MODELS_SUBMITTED, server_predictions, targets) are still on predictioncenter.org; total several GB. Selection filters (>=90% coverage, no internal gaps, MODELLER idealization) are described. The meta-predictor needs outputs of VERIFY3D, PROSA2003, PROVE, ANOLEA, BALA-SNAPP, TUNE, REFINER, PROQRES, several of which are no longer distributed; supplement holds only result figures/tables.

title: Analysis and comparison of very large metagenomes with fast clustering and functional annotation.
data_needed: GOS metagenome (7.7M Sanger reads, 44 samples) + Biomes set (Dinsdale 2008, 14.6M 454 reads, 45 metagenomes); Pfam/TIGRFAM/COG
where: NCBI BioProject PRJNA13694 (GOS); MG-RAST (Biomes); camera.calit2.net (gone)
note: CAMERA, the original host, is gone. GOS is in NCBI (PRJNA13694) and the Biomes metagenomes are in MG-RAST, but the read-level downloads were not tested. Family databases have drifted. The data are very large.

title: Automated confidence ranked classification of randomized controlled trial articles: an aid to evidence-based medicine.
data_needed: all human-related MEDLINE citations 1987-2012 (title, abstract, MeSH, publication type RCT as label)
where: PubMed E-utilities / annual MEDLINE baseline (current)
note: PubMed is public, but the 2012-era records and RCT publication-type and MeSH annotations have since been corrected. Older baselines are not distributed, so labels will drift. The manual review set is not provided. Very large.

title: WebArray: an online platform for microarray data analysis.
data_needed: none: web platform wrapping limma/affy; no dataset-based results reported
note: Software-platform description with screenshots; there is no quantitative analysis tied to an input dataset, so there is nothing to reproduce beyond rebuilding a limma/affy web front end. Low value as a reproduction target.

title: Biomedical text mining and its applications.
data_needed: None: a tutorial/review article with no computational results
where: n/a (review; cited corpus compilation pages at hu-berlin.de and uchsc.edu are gone)
note: This is a PLoS Comput Biol review of biomedical text mining. It has no method or experiment to reproduce, so it is not a meaningful reproduction target. The dead links are lists of corpora and tools, not inputs.

title: Integrating sequence and structural biology with DAS.
data_needed: none: protocol extensions (DAS 1.53E) and registry; examples use live third-party DAS sources
note: Infrastructure/specification paper without dataset-based results. The DAS registry (dasregistry.org) is gone and most DAS servers were retired by EBI/Ensembl around 2015, so the demonstrated integrations cannot be repeated; nothing to reimplement against.

title: RegNetwork: an integrated database of transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory networks in human and mouse.
data_needed: regulatory interactions collected from 25 source databases (TRED, KEGG, TRANSFAC, JASPAR, HPRD, BioGRID, miRBase, TarBase, miRecords, miRTarBase, TargetScan, PicTar, MicroCosm, microRNA.org, etc.; ~2013 releases) + TFBS motif scans
where: http://www.genome.jp/kegg/; http://jaspar.genereg.net/; http://thebiogrid.org/; http://www.mirbase.org/; http://www.microrna.gr/tarbase; http://www.targetscan.org/; http://pictar.mdc-berlin.de/; http://www.string-db.org; http://www.ebi.ac.uk/intact/
note: Database-integration paper; inputs are ~25 third-party resources at 2013-14 releases. Most live sources only serve newer releases. Unreachable/gone today: HPRD, miRecords, MicroCosm (EBI enright-srv), microRNA.org, old miRTarBase URL (moved), TRED indeterminate, TRANSFAC is commercial. RegNetwork's own site regnetworkweb.org returns Cloudflare 522, so the integrated network itself cannot be downloaded here. Exact rebuild not possible; an approximate rebuild from current releases is.

title: The power of protein interaction networks for associating genes with diseases.
data_needed: HPRD Release 7 human PPI network (8776 proteins/35820 edges main component) + OPHID network + OMIM morbidmap (2008) + UniProt gene loci/linkage intervals
where: HPRD (hprd.org: 503, down); OPHID superseded by IID (iid.ophid.utoronto.ca, alive, newer data); OMIM morbidmap (omim.org, registration required, current version only); btq076_1.pdf (supplementary figures only)
note: HPRD Release 7 is not available from its official site (503 maintenance page; HPRD stopped at Release 9 in 2010). OPHID now lives on as IID with much larger, newer content. Current OMIM morbidmap needs free registration; the 2008 snapshot is not archived. Project page cbcb.umd.edu/DiseaseNet is gone (404). Supplement holds result figures only. Can be redone approximately with current networks, but published numbers will not be reproduced exactly.

title: Identifying gene-disease associations using centrality on a literature mined gene-interaction network.
data_needed: 15 OMIM prostate-cancer seed genes (Table 1) + PubMed abstracts (2007) mined into a gene-interaction network; AIMed corpus for training the extractor
where: OMIM Morbid Map (license); PubMed E-utilities; AIMed via https://github.com/metalrt/ppi-dataset; gin.ncibi.org (unreachable)
note: The seed genes are in the paper. The mined network (GIN) is gone, and the 2007 PubMed snapshot, the dependency parser and SVM extraction would have to be redone, so results will drift. AIMed original ftp is untestable but a mirror exists. The evaluation relied on manual literature checks.

title: Epitopia: a web-server for predicting B-cell epitopes.
data_needed: 66 antibody-antigen co-crystal structures with epitopes and 194 sequence epitopes (Epitopia training data, Rubinstein et al. 2009)
where: http://epitopia.tau.ac.il/trainData (unreachable); RCSB PDB; Ponomarenko & Bourne 2007 benchmark (PMC2174481) and ElliPro set (PMC2607291)
note: The exact training lists were on the server's /trainData page, which no longer answers (503; Wayback has a capture of the main site only checked at 2009). Structures themselves are in PDB, and the structure set is an update of the Ponomarenko/ElliPro benchmarks, so an approximation is possible; the 194 sequence epitopes (Bcipep-derived) cannot be recovered from the paper.

title: Protein threading using context-specific alignment potential.
data_needed: In-house protein pair sets from PDB (BC40, PDB25): 1800 training + 500 validation pairs with DeepAlign reference alignments; Set6K, Set4K, Set180K alignment benchmarks; 1000x6000 PDB25 threading set; CASP10 123 domains
where: PDB (rcsb.org, alive); CASP10 targets (predictioncenter.org/download_area/CASP10/, alive); raptorx.uchicago.edu/download/ (503, down)
note: Only the raw ingredients are public: PDB structures and CASP10 targets/domains. The exact pair lists (training/validation, Set6K, Set4K, Set180K, the 1000 targets, the PDB25 version) and the DeepAlign reference alignments are not in the paper or any supplement (there is none), and the RaptorX download site is down. The sets can be rebuilt by their published criteria, but not identically. Heavy compute (179k pairs, HHpred profiles).

title: MAPPER: a search engine for the computational identification of putative transcription factor binding sites in multiple genomes.
data_needed: binding-site alignments from TRANSFAC (public release ~7.0) and JASPAR used to build 1,079 HMMs; genomic promoter sequences of 5 genomes
where: http://jaspar.genereg.net/ (current JASPAR sites); 1471-2105-6-79-S2.xls (evaluation results); TRANSFAC public 7.0 no longer distributed
note: 990 of the HMMs came from TRANSFAC site sequences. gene-regulation.com still offers the free 'TRANSFAC 7.0 Public 2005' snapshot (registration; not downloaded), which may differ from the release used; current TRANSFAC is commercial. JASPAR (89 alignments) only in much newer releases. Supplement S2 holds evaluation results, S1 only links to the dead mapper.chip.org site. Genomes needed in 2005 assemblies (old UCSC builds still downloadable).

title: lncRNome: a comprehensive knowledgebase of human long noncoding RNAs.
data_needed: GENCODE v12 lncRNAs + UCSC sequences, dbSNP 135, NIH Roadmap methylation/histone data, Ago PAR-CLIP (HEK293), deepBase small-RNA clusters, lncRNAdb, plus manually curated literature annotations
where: GENCODE release_12 (ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_12/, alive); Roadmap (egg2.wustl.edu/roadmap, alive); lncRNAdb (lncrnadb.org, alive); deepBase (rna.sysu.edu.cn, 403); UCSC hg19 snp135 (removed; snp138+ only); genome.igib.res.in/lncRNome (503, down); supp_bat034_Supplementary_Methods.docx (parameters only)
note: This is a database paper; the 'result' is the lncRNome database itself, which is offline (only the homepage has a Wayback capture). Most automated inputs are public (GENCODE v12 still on the EBI FTP; Roadmap; PAR-CLIP in GEO). dbSNP 135 is no longer in the UCSC hg19 tables. The manually curated disease/interaction annotations and the in-house SVM protein-binding predictions are not available. Little algorithmic content to reproduce.

title: NOXclass: prediction of protein-protein interaction types.
data_needed: 243 PDB protein-protein interfaces (obligate / non-obligate / crystal packing) compiled from Bradford&Westhead 2005, ProMate (Neuvirth 2004) and Ponstingl/Valdar crystal-contact sets
where: PMC supplement 1471-2105-7-27-S1.pdf (results only); source lists in cited papers' supplements; RCSB PDB
note: The supplement has only LOOCV result tables. The 243-interaction BNCP-CS list is not given and was on the gone noxclass site (archived). It could be rebuilt from the cited source sets plus redundancy filtering, but not exactly. PDB coordinates and NACCESS are needed.

title: BARCRAWL and BARTAB: software tools for the design and implementation of barcoded primers for highly multiplexed DNA sequencing.
data_needed: barcode design needs only primer/adapter sequences given in the paper; validation used 454 reads from 47 barcoded LSU559R primers on metagenomic DNA
where: paper text (primer sequences, design parameters)
note: Software-tool paper. The barcode-design algorithm can be re-run from parameters in the paper, but the pyrosequencing validation reads (~29,000 reads) were never deposited (no SRA accession), so the bartab polishing and barcode-bias results cannot be reproduced. phyloware.com is gone.

title: miTarget: microRNA target gene prediction using a support vector machine.
data_needed: literature-curated miRNA:target-site training set (152 positives, 246 negatives incl. 163 inferred) + Ensembl human 3'UTRs + Lim et al. 2005 miR-1/miR-124 transfection microarray gene lists
where: 1471-2105-7-411-S1.xls (source papers, miRNA and gene names); Ensembl; Rfam/miRBase; Lim et al. 2005 (GEO GSE2075)
note: S1 lists only the source papers and miRNA/gene pairs (checked), not the curated binding-site alignments or the deletion-derived negatives; those were on the dead cbit.snu.ac.kr/~miTarget site (Wayback capture exists, not downloadable here). Re-curation from ~10 papers is possible but would not give the exact 398 examples. Old Ensembl 3'UTR set (20,008 seqs) only as newer releases.

title: Positive-unlabeled learning for disease gene identification.
data_needed: Disease gene benchmark (GeneCards + OMIM, 5405 genes/2751 phenotypes, 2012 versions) + GO BP/MF/CC annotations + Pfam domains + HPRD/OPHID human PPI (143,939 PPIs) + ~16k Ensembl genes as unlabeled set
where: GO (geneontology.org, alive; archived releases); Pfam releases (ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/Pfam/releases/, alive); OMIM (registration); GeneCards (403 to scripts, licensed); HPRD (503, down); OPHID -> IID (newer); supp_bts504 docx (feature tables only)
note: Neither the disease gene benchmark nor the positive/unlabeled gene lists are provided; the supplement only lists top GO and domain features. GeneCards bulk data is licensed, and OMIM needs registration and gives only current data. HPRD is offline, and OPHID has been replaced by IID. GO and Pfam have dated archives, so features can be rebuilt approximately. The project page (i2r.a-star.edu.sg/~xlli/PUDI) is gone. Only an approximate rerun is possible.

title: Predicting protein contact map using evolutionary and physical constraints by integer programming.
data_needed: PDB25-derived training proteins (pre-May 2012) + Set600 test set (PDB25, <25% identity) + CASP10 targets; features from PSI-BLAST profiles and predicted secondary structure
where: PDB (rcsb.org, alive); CASP10 targets and structures (predictioncenter.org/download_area/CASP10/, alive); raptorx.uchicago.edu (503, down)
note: CASP10 targets and native structures are public, so the CASP10 evaluation can be redone. The training protein list and the Set600 IDs are not given (there is no supplement), and the RaptorX site that might have hosted them is down. Set600 can only be rebuilt approximately from PDB25 using the stated filters. Requires CPLEX (academic licence) for the ILP, plus an evolutionary-coupling (EVfold-style) input.

title: Designing focused chemical libraries enriched in protein-protein interaction inhibitors using machine-learning methods.
data_needed: 66 + 26 literature PPI inhibitors, 557 DrugBank small molecules (non-PPI), 2,000 ChemBridge diversity decoys, Dragon descriptors, 10 PubChem PPI bioassays
where: pcbi.1000695.s001.tif and s003.tif (structure drawings of the 66 and 26 PPI inhibitors); DrugBank; PubChem BioAssay (e.g. AID1434); http://www.chembridge.com
note: PPI inhibitors exist only as images of chemical structures (must be redrawn as SMILES). The 557 DrugBank molecules were picked by fingerprint clustering and are not listed; the 2,000 ChemBridge decoys are an unlisted subset of a commercial library. Descriptors came from E-Dragon (alive but Dragon is commercial). PubChem assays are public. The authors' later 2P2I database was not checked.

title: Assessing drug target association using semantic linked data.
data_needed: Chem2Bio2RDF/SLAP semantic network (~290k nodes, 720k edges) built from PubChem, DrugBank, ChEMBL, BindingDB, KEGG, CTD, SIDER, HPRD, OMIM, GOA, HGNC; MATADOR + CMap for validation
where: chem2bio2rdf.org (503); supplements s007/s008/s012 (node/edge source counts), s010/s011 (results); current DrugBank, ChEMBL, SIDER, CTD (alive); HPRD (503)
