note: The integrated network is not available (chem2bio2rdf.org returns 503). The supplement gives source and edge-type counts but not the data. Most sources are alive in much newer versions, but HPRD and SuperTarget/MATADOR (insilico.charite.de, DNS fails) are not. A rebuild would differ substantially.

title: FIGENIX: intelligent automation of genomic annotation: expertise integration in a new software platform.
data_needed: modified HMR195 set (55 mouse/rat genomic sequences) + human Swiss-Prot for the gene-prediction comparison; amphioxus cosmids and Ciona scaffolds for case studies
where: HMR195 (Rogic et al. 2001; GenBank accessions, https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~rogic/evaluation/ returns 403); UniProt/Swiss-Prot (current only)
note: Platform/expert-system paper; the only quantitative result (Table 6) uses a 'modified version' of HMR195 whose modifications are not given. HMR195 sequences can be refetched from GenBank but the authors' 55-sequence subset is not listed. Swiss-Prot of 2005 only as old UniProt releases. Little to reproduce beyond pipeline orchestration.

title: IDconverter and IDClight: conversion and annotation of gene and protein IDs.
data_needed: Pregenerated ID-mapping tables from 2006 Ensembl, UniGene, NCBI (Entrez Gene/PubMed), UCSC chromosomal locations, KEGG, Reactome + test ID lists (random 10-10,000 subsets of HG-U133A probes, HUGO symbols, Entrez Gene IDs, RefSeq release 18 NM_ IDs, drawn 24 Aug 2006)
where: 1471-2105-8-9-S2.pdf (test-set recipe); RefSeq-release18.catalog.gz (ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/refseq/release/release-catalog/archive/, alive); Ensembl 2006 releases (ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-40/, alive); UniGene final dump (ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/repository/UniGene/, alive but retired 2019); test files at idconverter.bioinfo.cnio.es/help/test-files.html (gone; archived)
note: The exact random test lists were only on the dead CNIO site (a Wayback capture of the homepage exists; test files not checked). Their sources can be rebuilt from 2006-era archives: RefSeq release 18 catalog, Ensembl ~v40, and the final UniGene dump (the 2006 UniGene build itself is not kept). KEGG is licensed, and the old gene_info and HUGO dumps are not archived. The comparison tools (SOURCE, MatchMiner, Onto-Translate) are mostly offline, so the timing/coverage comparison cannot be redone.

title: Relemed: sentence-level search engine with relevance score for the MEDLINE database of biomedical articles.
data_needed: full MEDLINE citation set (~16 million records, ~2006) split into sentences + UMLS for term mapping; example queries compared with PubMed
where: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/baseline/ (current baseline only); UMLS (licence); 1472-6947-7-1-S1.pdf; 1472-6947-7-1-S2.pdf
note: Search-engine paper. NLM distributes only the current annual MEDLINE baseline (tens of GB), so the 2006 snapshot is not available; the evaluation is a few illustrative queries with author judgments (S2 PDF), not a reusable test set. UMLS requires a licence. A reimplementation is possible on today's MEDLINE but the numbers will differ.

title: PhyME: a probabilistic algorithm for finding motifs in sets of orthologous sequences.
data_needed: synthetic planted-motif sequences + yeast SCPD regulons with 800 bp promoters and Cliften 2003 orthologs (S. mikatae, S. kudriavzevii, S. bayanus) + 9 fly enhancers (D. melanogaster/D. pseudoobscura) + 2 human datasets with mouse/rat orthologs (Tompa assessment)
where: https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/sgd-archive.yeastgenome.org/?prefix=sequence/fungi/ (WashU 2003 Cliften assemblies); RSAT for S. cerevisiae upstream sequences; SCPD (http://rulai.cshl.edu/SCPD/ now redirects elsewhere)
note: Synthetic data is fully specified (parameters in text). SCPD, which supplied the regulon gene lists, known sites and weight matrices, is gone; the 2003 sensu-stricto assemblies are still in the SGD archive. The Tompa et al. assessment site (bio.cs.washington.edu) no longer resolves. Fly enhancer coordinates must be re-derived. Only the synthetic part is cleanly reproducible.

title: Predicting protein-protein interface residues using local surface structural similarity.
data_needed: repository of surface structural elements from all PDB interacting chains (ProtInDB, Feb 2011; ProtInDB-PQS intersection) + benchmarks DS24Carl, DS188 (Docking Benchmark 3.0), DS56bound/DS56unbound (CAPRI)
where: RCSB PDB (biological assemblies; cited PDB IDs resolve); Docking Benchmark 3.0; benchmark chain lists in Carl et al. 2008 and Zhang et al. 2010 (PredUs); 1471-2105-13-41-S1.PDF (method details)
note: The repository can be rebuilt from PDB with a Feb-2011 release-date cutoff (tens of GB of structures), but ProtInDB (Iowa State) and PQS (retired by EBI) are gone, so the ProtInDB-PQS repository and PQS-derived interface labels of DS188/DS56 cannot be reproduced exactly. The supplement PDF has parameters and extra results only.

title: Resolving structural variability in network models and the brain.
data_needed: Diffusion spectrum imaging structural connectomes of 5 healthy subjects, 998 cortical ROIs (Hagmann et al. 2008) with ROI coordinates, compared against 13 synthetic network models
where: Synthetic models fully specified in the paper and Text S1 (pcbi.1003491.s007.pdf); pcbi.1003491.s005/s006.pdf (fitted parameters and diagnostic means = results); Hagmann 2008 connectomes not located in any public repository
note: All 13 synthetic generators are specified (with fitted parameters in S5), but the empirical comparison needs the Hagmann et al. 2008 998-ROI DSI connectomes plus node coordinates. These come from a separate study, are not deposited with this paper, and a web search did not find a public copy (distributed on request). A substitute such as the Lausanne multi-scale DSI connectomes would only reproduce trends. The Gleich programs link (stanford.edu/~dgleich/programs) is gone.

title: MRFalign: protein homology detection through alignment of Markov random fields.
data_needed: 1,400 SCOP training pairs; Set3.6K and Set2.6K test pairs (RaptorX benchmarks) with reference structure alignments; SCOP20/40/80 sets with HHpred MSAs (Soeding group); PSI-BLAST/nr profiles
where: https://scop.berkeley.edu/downloads/scopseq-1.73/ (ASTRAL subsets to rebuild SCOP20/40); ftp://toolkit.genzentrum.lmu.de/pub/ (gone); http://raptorx.uchicago.edu/download/ (unreachable)
note: The training pairs and Set3.6K/Set2.6K lists were only on the RaptorX download site (503 / connection reset). The Soeding SCOP20/40/80 MSA files were on toolkit.genzentrum.lmu.de, which no longer resolves; SCOPe still hosts ASTRAL 1.73/1.75 subsets so similar sets can be rebuilt (80% subset needs custom filtering) but MSAs must be regenerated against today's databases.

title: CATHEDRAL: a fast and effective algorithm to predict folds and domain boundaries from multidomain protein structures.
data_needed: CATH v2.6.0 / SCOP 1.65 consensus domain benchmark (6,003 SRep domains, 907 fold groups) + multidomain chain test set
where: https://download.cathdb.info/cath/releases/all-releases/v2_6_0/ (classification, nr sets, sequences); SCOPe archive (SCOP 1.65 parseable files); RCSB PDB
note: Both old releases still exist (the CATH v2.6.0 directory and SCOP 1.65 at SCOPe), but the specific benchmark domain and chain lists were never published. The supplement is just a CATH description. Rebuilding the consensus set is laborious and approximate.

title: Application of change point analysis to daily influenza-like illness emergency department visits.
data_needed: daily ILI emergency-department visit counts for four contiguous US states from the ISDS DiSTRIBUTE network (2009 H1N1 period) + simulated autocorrelated time series
where: http://isdsdistribute.org (unreachable); supp_amiajnl-2011-000793_amiajnl-2011-000793-s1.pdf (method appendix only); https://sites.google.com/site/changepointanalysis (CUSUM programs)
note: The simulation study (100-point series at varying autocorrelation rho) is specified in the text and can be redone. The real DiSTRIBUTE ILI series were aggregated from state/local health departments and were never released as files; the project site no longer answers. The authors' Google Sites page with R/SAS/Stata CUSUM code is still alive (code, not data).

title: SNPdetector: a software tool for sensitive and accurate SNP detection.
data_needed: PCR-resequencing trace files: mouse 25 inbred strains (93 amplicons, 40 kb), human HapMap ENCODE regions (48 individuals), zebrafish; reference sequences and primers; genotyping results for validation
where: NCBI SRA (former Trace Archive; https://trace.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Traces/trace.cgi says it is retired and records are searchable in SRA); dbSNP; pcbi.0010053.st001.pdf (parameters)
note: The paper gives no trace accessions. HapMap ENCODE resequencing traces were deposited in the Trace Archive, which NCBI has retired into SRA (could not identify the specific NCI runs). The mouse and zebrafish trace sets and the curated 1,201-SNP mouse benchmark are not provided. Supplements are figures and the parameter table only. lpg.nci.nih.gov is gone.

title: Assessing protein similarity with Gene Ontology and its use in subnuclear localization prediction.
data_needed: Nuclear Protein Database (NPD) proteins in 6 subnuclear compartments (from authors' earlier dataset) + GO annotations; multi-localization test set
where: 1471-2105-7-491-S1.xls (IDs + compartment GO annotations for 71/116 single-localization proteins); NPD (npd.hgu.mrc.ac.uk now redirects to IGC homepage)
note: NPD is gone. The supplement lists only the GO-annotated subset of proteins, not the full 6-compartment dataset (Table 1 counts) or the multi-localization test set. GO annotations have changed a lot since 2006.

title: An SVM-based system for predicting protein subnuclear localizations.
data_needed: Vertebrate nuclear proteins with 6 subnuclear localizations extracted from the Nuclear Protein Database (NPD; single-localization set reduced to <50% identity with PROSET) + independent multi-localization test set
where: 1471-2105-6-291-S1.doc (Table S1: ~90 multi-localization test proteins, SwissProt/Entrez IDs with reported compartments); NPD (npd.hgu.mrc.ac.uk, now redirects to an Edinburgh IGC redirect page = gone); array.bioengr.uic.edu/subnuclear.htm (503)
note: Only the independent multi-localization test set is recoverable: its UniProt/RefSeq IDs are in the S1 table, so sequences can be fetched, though some IDs may be merged or obsolete. The main LOOCV training set (single-localization proteins from NPD after PROSET filtering) is not listed, and NPD no longer exists. A rebuild from UniProt subcellular-location annotations would be a different dataset.

title: Predicting changes in protein thermostability brought about by single- or multi-site mutations.
data_needed: M-dataset (3366 single/multi-site mutants from ProTherm) + S-dataset; PDB structures; FoldX/Modeller features
where: ProTherm (abren.net: 503); ProThermDB https://web.iitm.ac.in/bioinfo2/prothermdb/ (alive, re-curated); mobioinfor.cn/prethermut/download.htm (unreachable); RCSB PDB
note: The curated M- and S-datasets were only on the unreachable Prethermut download page. The original ProTherm is down, and ProThermDB is a re-curated successor that will not reproduce the 3366-mutant selection exactly. The supplement DOC holds only result tables.

title: Predicting deleterious nsSNPs: an analysis of sequence and structural attributes.
data_needed: ~14.6k nsSNPs from Swiss-Prot VARIANT pages (2005) mapped to Ensembl (10,419 disease / 4217 polymorphism) with structural/PSIC features
where: https://ftp.uniprot.org/pub/databases/uniprot/knowledgebase/complete/docs/humsavar.txt (current); UniProt previous releases (2005 release not verified); Ensembl archives
note: Only the current humsavar is confirmed (8.7 MB); it is much larger and relabelled since 2005. The authors' dataset and DAS site (brightstudy.ac.uk) are gone. Ensembl 2005 archives are not easily usable.

title: A two-stage approach for improved prediction of residue contact maps.
data_needed: December 2003 25% PDB_select chains (1,275 train / 327 test after removing >200 aa) + PSI-BLAST profiles + Porter secondary-structure predictions; contacts from PDB coordinates
where: RCSB PDB (structures); PDBselect archive (https://bioinfo.thm.de/pdbselect/ gives 502 here; old host bioinfo.tg.fh-giessen.de gone); http://distill.ucd.ie (unreachable)
note: Structures are in PDB, but the exact Dec-2003 25% PDB_select list and the train/test split are not given in the paper and the PDBselect and Distill sites could not be reached. A similar set can be rebuilt (e.g. PISCES/PDB_select current lists with a date cutoff) but results will not be directly comparable. Profiles depend on 2004-era nr.

title: FUNYBASE: a FUNgal phYlogenomic dataBASE.
data_needed: 30 fungal proteomes (2007 annotations from Broad FGI, JGI, NCBI, SGD, Genolevures, NITE, etc.) + all-vs-all BLAST + Tribe-MCL clustering
where: http://www.broad.mit.edu/annotation/fungi/fgi/ (redirects); http://genome.jgi-psf.org/ (JGI MycoCosm); NCBI Genomes; SGD fungal archive; http://micans.org/mcl
note: Database paper; its outputs (246 single-copy ortholog families, alignments, trees) were on genome.jouy.inra.fr/funybase (unreachable). Most of the 30 genomes are still obtainable from NCBI/JGI, but many have been re-annotated since 2007 (version drift) and some portals cited (AGD, NITE, fungalgenomes.org) are gone. Rebuild is possible only approximately.

title: INTREPID--INformation-theoretic TREe traversal for Protein functional site IDentification.
data_needed: CSA-100 / CSA-71 enzyme families (Catalytic Site Atlas) with large divergent MSAs and trees from PhyloFacts/FlowerPower; Capra&Singh 2008 SDP dataset
where: M-CSA https://www.ebi.ac.uk/thornton-srv/m-csa/ (current); btn474_1.pdf (supplementary results); phylogenomics.berkeley.edu (gone, archived)
note: The alignments and trees, which are the actual input, came from PhyloFacts and are gone. CSA has been replaced by M-CSA with different annotations, and the 100 family list is not in the supplement. The alignments would have to be rebuilt with UniProt-based pipelines.

title: A two-layered machine learning method to identify protein O-GlcNAcylation sites with O-GlcNAc transferase substrate motifs.
data_needed: 410 non-redundant experimentally verified O-GlcNAc sites (dbOGAP 392, O-GlycBase v6.0 24, UniProtKB) on 176 proteins + negative S/T fragments from the same proteins; independent test set of 1,361 PhosphoSitePlus O-GlcNAc sites
where: 1471-2105-16-S18-S10-S1/S2/S3.pdf (amino-acid grouping, motif logos with group counts, comparison figure; no site lists); dbOGAP (dbogap.org / oglcnac.mcw.edu: no connection); OGlycBase moved page points to services.healthtech.dtu.dk (404); UniProtKB (alive); PhosphoSitePlus (alive, free registration for downloads); OGTSite (503)
note: The 410 training sites are not listed anywhere (S2 only shows motif logos and cluster sizes). dbOGAP, the main source (392 of 410 sites), is offline, and OGlycBase v6.0 has disappeared from DTU. UniProtKB and PhosphoSitePlus are live but current; old releases of these exact entries cannot be recovered. A modern O-GlcNAc set (e.g., O-GlcNAc Atlas) would be a different benchmark.

title: MetaRoute: fast search for relevant metabolic routes for interactive network navigation and visualization.
data_needed: KEGG metabolic data (~7,000 reactions, compounds, organism enzyme lists, ~2008) imported via BNDB/BN++, with KEGG RPAIR-style atom mapping rules (Arita 2003)
where: btn360_1.pdf (algorithm details and timing comparison only); KEGG (current, REST API free for academic use, FTP by subscription; RPAIR discontinued 2016, replaced by RCLASS); MetaRoute service at uni-tuebingen.de (gone; archived)
note: The input network is a 2008 KEGG snapshot with atom-mapping rules. KEGG RPAIR no longer exists, and the 2008 snapshot is not available. A comparable network can be built from current KEGG RCLASS or MetaCyc/Rhea atom mappings, but route lengths and timings will differ. The paper shows example routes but no fixed benchmark list.

title: Functional discrimination of membrane proteins using machine learning techniques.
data_needed: TCDB-derived transporters (510 channels/pores, 502 electrochemical, 706 active; 1718 total) + 3336 non-transporters
where: https://www.tcdb.org/download.php (current TCDB); tmbeta-genome.cbrc.jp/disc-function (gone)
note: TCDB is alive but has grown and been reorganised since 2007, and the curated 1718/3336 sets are not available. Features are just amino acid composition, so a re-derived dataset is cheap but not identical.

title: Correlated mutations: a hallmark of phenotypic amino acid substitutions.
data_needed: all HGMD disease-causing missense mutations (c. 2009, HGMD Professional) mapped to human proteins with >=30 diverse orthologs (MSAs) + Swiss-Prot functional-site features + benign substitution set
where: HGMD (http://www.hgmd.cf.ac.uk redirects to an outage page; Professional is licensed via biobase/QIAGEN); UniProt/Swiss-Prot features; pcbi.1000923.s001.pdf (supplementary analysis); http://webclu.bio.wzw.tum.de/~pagel/supplements/correlated-positions/ (unreachable)
note: The mutation set comes from licensed HGMD Professional; the public HGMD site was down when checked. The authors' supplement site with the correlated-position data is unreachable. ClinVar/UniProt humsavar could substitute, but results would differ. Ortholog/MSA construction is described, not provided.

title: DT-Web: a web-based application for drug-target interaction and drug combination prediction through domain-tuned network-based inference.
data_needed: DrugBank drug-target interactions (2014-15 release) + drug chemical similarity and target sequence similarity matrices + Homo sapiens Reactome and NCI-PID pathways in BioPAX L3 via Pathway Commons PC2
where: Pathway Commons archives v3-v14 (download.baderlab.org/PathwayCommons/PC2/, alive; includes PID-era releases); DrugBank (go.drugbank.com: account/licence, current release only); alpha.dmi.unict.it/dtweb/ (503; Wayback capture exists)
note: This web-application paper has no benchmark data in a supplement (there is none). The DrugBank snapshot the DT-Hybrid predictions came from is not identified and cannot be retrieved without an account (current release only). Dated Pathway Commons releases are archived, so the multi-pathway environment can be approximately rebuilt. The case-study gene lists are in the text only.

title: Biomedical question answering using semantic relations.
data_needed: SemRep semantic relations from all MEDLINE (21M citations, 122M sentences) + expert judgments of 7,510 relation instances by 80 evaluators
where: SemMedDB https://lhncbc.nlm.nih.gov/ii/tools/SemRep_SemMedDB_SKR/SemMedDB_download.html (UMLS license; newer releases); sembt.mf.uni-lj.si (unreachable, archived)
note: Relation extraction can be approximated with current SemMedDB, which needs a UMLS licence and is a newer SemRep version. The expert evaluation judgments behind the accuracy results are not available.

title: Predicting mostly disordered proteins by using structure-unknown protein data.
data_needed: DisProt 3.3 disordered proteins + PDB ordered proteins (608 evaluation sequences) + UniRef50 (UniProt 48.9) unlabeled sequences
where: https://disprot.org/download (current releases only); UniProt previous releases (2006 not verified); RCSB PDB; mbs.cbrc.jp/poodle (gone, archived)
note: The 608-sequence evaluation set is not published, and DisProt 3.3 is not offered on the current site. The 2006 UniRef50 snapshot is not verified as available. Rebuilding with current DisProt changes the data substantially.

title: A feature-based approach to modeling protein-DNA interactions.
data_needed: Harbison 2004 yeast ChIP-chip binding data; two human TFBS datasets (refs 10, 13); compiled human/mouse TF ChIP-chip/ChIP-seq/ChIP-PET target sets; synthetic data
where: Harbison 2004 data (fraenkel.mit.edu/Harbison/release_v24/ now 404); GEO for individual ChIP studies; genie.weizmann.ac.il (gone, archived)
note: The supplements are methods and result figures. The compiled TF target and background sequence sets were on the gone lab site. The Harbison data have moved from their original page, and the mammalian ChIP compilation would need rebuilding study by study. The synthetic part is reproducible.

title: L2-norm multiple kernel learning and its application to biomedical data fusion.
data_needed: Exp1: 9 genomic data sources (Endeavour-style) for 620 genes / 29 OMIM diseases; Exp2: prostate cancer gene prioritization; Exp3: rectal cancer patients (36, microarray + proteomics); Exp4: clinical endometrial (339), miscarriage (2,356) and pregnancy (856) datasets; Exp5: UCI pen-digit and optical-digit
where: 1471-2105-11-309-S1.PDF (list of genomic sources, kernel definitions, per-source results); UCI pendigits/optdigits (archive.ics.uci.edu, alive); homes.esat.kuleuven.be/~sistawww/bioi/syu/l2lssvm.html (unreachable; archived)
note: Only the UCI timing experiment uses fully public data. The gene-prioritization kernels come from Endeavour data sources (2008-9 versions, not distributed as kernels), and the rectal cancer, endometrial, miscarriage and pregnancy clinical datasets are KU Leuven/UZ Leuven patient data with no public deposit. The MKL formulations are well specified, so the method can be reimplemented and tested on substitute public data, but not on the paper's data.

title: Secondary structure assignment that accurately reflects physical and evolutionary characteristics.
data_needed: Top500 high-resolution (<1.8 A) structure set (Lovell et al. 2003) + HOMSTRAD families for alignment tests
where: RCSB PDB; Top500 list (kinemage.biochem.duke.edu pages 404); HOMSTRAD (mizuguchilab.org/homstrad 404; old Cambridge host gone)
note: PDB entries are available, but the Top500 ID list and HOMSTRAD were not found at their known URLs. Copies of Top500 may exist in the 2003 paper supplement or in MolProbity distributions. The SEGNO site itself is unreachable.

title: Predicting cancer involvement of genes from heterogeneous data.
data_needed: known cancer-gene seed list + a PPI network built with PIANA (HPRD/BIND/etc.) + 24 Oncomine differential-expression cancer studies + sequence/structure/evolution gene features
where: 1471-2105-9-172-S6.pdf (list of the 24 Oncomine studies); 1471-2105-9-172-S7.txt (per-gene cancer linker degree, output); Oncomine (oncomine.org now redirects to a ThermoFisher product; free research version gone); PIANA (sbi.imim.es gone)
note: S7 is the scored-gene output; S6 only names the 24 Oncomine studies. Oncomine's free academic platform is gone (now commercial), so the exact differential-expression inputs are not retrievable as such, though many of the 24 underlying studies are individually in GEO. The PIANA-built interaction network and the scored_genes.tab.txt are gone. Rebuild would be approximate.

title: Functional genomics complements quantitative genetics in identifying disease-gene associations.
data_needed: integrated mouse functional relationship network (Bayesian integration of many GEO expression, PPI, phenotype, etc. datasets) + MGI mammalian phenotype annotations
where: MGI reports https://www.informatics.jax.org/downloads/reports/ (current); cbfg.jax.org/phenotype (gone, archived); supplements s002-s006 (results/methods)
note: The functional network, the real input to the SVMs, was on a gone JAX site, and its many component datasets are not enumerated in a downloadable form. MP annotations are current only. A rebuild is a large project.

title: Large-scale prediction of long disordered regions in proteins using random forests.
data_needed: DisProt 3.6 long disordered regions (352 regions) + PDBSelect25 (Oct 2008) ordered chains; blind tests Hirose-ADS1, Han-ADS1, Peng-DB
where: 1471-2105-10-8-S1.txt (Han-ADS1 FASTA, 86 regions); DisProt (current only); PDBselect host (DNS fails); Hirose-ADS1 / Peng-DB from POODLE-L and VLS2 papers
note: Only the Han-ADS1 blind set is in PMC. The training set (old DisProt plus PDBSelect25) and the other two blind sets are not, and the authors' FASTA link is gone. AAindex is reachable.

title: Predicting residue contacts using pragmatic correlated mutations method: reducing the false positives.
data_needed: 15 optimisation + 65 benchmark high-resolution PDB structures (Dunbrack PISCES) with PSI-BLAST homologs from nr
where: RCSB PDB; https://dunbrack.fccc.edu/pisces/ (alive, current culls); NCBI nr
note: The structure lists are not given in the paper, which has no tables, or in a supplement. PISCES now returns different culls, and homolog sets from today's nr will differ. The site ces.clemson.edu/compbio/recon is gone.

title: A dynamic network approach for the study of human phenotypes.
data_needed: Patient-level Medicare (MedPAR) hospital claims 1990-1993, ~13M patients aged 65+, ICD-9-CM diagnoses with demographics and death dates
where: http://hudine.neu.edu/resource/data/data.html (derived PDN tables; host unreachable); pcbi.1000353.s001.doc (methods text only)
note: Raw input is restricted CMS Medicare claims (DUA via ResDAC, not public). The derived comorbidity tables (RR/phi for 18 subsets) were released at hudine.neu.edu, which now times out; only the homepage has a Wayback capture. Supplement is a 19-page Word methods/description document with no data. Reproduction needs new access to CMS data.

title: StAR: a simple tool for the statistical comparison of ROC curves.
data_needed: none specific: tool takes user ROC score files; validated on unpublished protein-structure-error classifier scores
note: This is a software note implementing the DeLong nonparametric AUC comparison. The validation data (classifier scores from the authors' earlier studies) were never released. The method itself can be checked on any paired ROC data, e.g. against pROC, so the missing data matter less than the status suggests.

title: Computational identification of ubiquitylation sites from protein sequences.
data_needed: UBIDATA: 157 ubiquitylation sites + 3676 non-sites from 105 UbiProt proteins; 3424-site independent set
where: UbiProt (ubiprot.org.ru: DNS fails); iclab.life.nctu.edu.tw/ubipred (unreachable, archived)
note: UbiProt is gone and the dataset was only on the UbiPred site, which has a Wayback capture that was not checked from here. There is no PMC supplement. The 31 AAindex properties are listed in Table 1. Later ubiquitination papers may have reused UBIDATA.

title: Windows .NET Network Distributed Basic Local Alignment Search Toolkit (W.ND-BLAST).
data_needed: Unspecified in-house query sets (up to 1500 nucleotide sequences, BLASTx) against an unspecified 332 MB protein database and a 1.5 GB subset of NCBI nt; 12-15-04 NCBI nr/nt snapshots
where: NCBI BLAST databases (ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/blast/db, current only); liru.ars.usda.gov (unreachable)
note: This paper benchmarks a distributed-computing tool (wall-clock speedup on lab Windows PCs). Neither the query sequences nor the custom databases are identified, and the December 2004 nr/nt snapshots are not archived by NCBI. Timings depend on 2004 hardware anyway. The speedup experiment can be repeated with any public sequences, but the published numbers are not reproducible.

title: MIDAS: software for analysis and visualisation of interallelic disequilibrium between multiallelic markers.
data_needed: example genotype set: microsatellites + SNPs from chromosome 11p (Zapata et al. in prep, 50 samples)
note: This is a software paper, and its example data were unpublished. The LD estimators (Hill EM, D', r2) can be tested on simulated or public multiallelic genotypes instead.

title: SNPAnalyzer 2.0: a web-based integrated workbench for linkage disequilibrium analysis and association analysis.
data_needed: HLA-region true haplotypes from dbSNP (African American n=72, Asian American n=75) + simulated case/control genotype sets (100-100,000 SNPs, 1000+1000 samples) for comparison with Haploview/PLINK/BEAGLE
where: 1471-2105-9-290-S1.doc (one-paragraph description only); test datasets at snp.istech21.com/snpanalyzer/2.0/ (gone; homepage has Wayback capture); dbSNP (alive, but submitter haplotype records no longer served)
note: The authors' test datasets were hosted only on the dead tool site. The dbSNP HLA haplotype submission is not identified (no ss/batch ID), and dbSNP no longer serves population haplotype data. The simulation procedure is not specified well enough to regenerate identical genotypes. Any public phased panel (1000 Genomes HLA region) could stand in to compare LD blocks and timings.

title: Hydra: software for tailored processing of H/D exchange data from MS or tandem MS analyses.
data_needed: H/DX-MS raw data for tubulin and calmodulin test projects (MS and MS/MS)
note: This is a software paper. The raw instrument files used for validation were never released, and no repository accession is given.

title: NBA-Palm: prediction of palmitoylation site implemented in Naïve Bayes algorithm.
data_needed: Literature-curated palmitoylation sites: old CSS-Palm set (210 sites/83 proteins) and new non-redundant set (245 sites/105 proteins, curated to 31 Mar 2006) with Swiss-Prot/TrEMBL sequences
where: Data 'available upon request' only; NBA-Palm site (bioinfo.tsinghua.edu.cn/NBA-Palm: no connection; archived); CSS-Palm site (csspalm.biocuckoo.org alive, but download.php 404)
note: The paper says the curated dataset is available only on request, and there is no supplement. The site lists are not in the text. Modern resources (UniProt lipidation features, SwissPalm) contain these sites and many more, but the 2006 non-redundant set cannot be rebuilt exactly. The naive Bayes window classifier itself is trivial.

title: Improving protein fold recognition by random forest.
data_needed: FOLDpro benchmark derived from Lindahl's dataset (976 SCOP 1.39 proteins, <=40% identity; all-against-all pairs with FOLDpro pairwise features from alignment/profile/structure tools)
where: SCOPe downloads (scop.berkeley.edu, alive; parseable releases start at 1.48, no 1.39); calla.rnet.missouri.edu/rf-fold/ (404; Wayback capture exists); FOLDpro data not on the UCI IGB download server
note: RF-Fold was trained on precomputed FOLDpro pairwise feature vectors. Neither those nor the Lindahl 976-protein list are in the paper (there is no supplement), and SCOP 1.39 is not distributed by SCOPe. Recomputing the ~84 FOLDpro features would need many legacy tools (PSI-BLAST, HMMER, CLUSTALW, PRC, SSpro...). An archived copy of the RF-Fold site might hold data, but this was not checked.

title: JCoast - a biologist-centric software tool for data mining and comparison of prokaryotic (meta)genomes.
data_needed: GenDB-format (meta)genome annotation databases used for demonstration
where: megx.net/jcoast (gone, archived)
note: This is a GUI and API software paper with no quantitative results. The demo GenDB projects were not distributed, and GEO GPL3 cited in the dossier does not resolve. It is a poor reproduction target.

title: Saliva Ontology: an ontology-based framework for a Salivaomics Knowledge Base.
data_needed: None computed: an ontology design paper (Saliva Ontology SALO, built from UCLA salivaomics resources and OBO Foundry ontologies)
where: skb.ucla.edu/SALO/ (404); BioPortal SALO page (403 to scripts; API needs key); not in OLS or OBO Foundry
note: There are no computational results to reproduce; the product is the ontology itself. It was supposed to be released on NCBO BioPortal, but this could not be verified (403 page; the API requires a key). It is not in OLS or the OBO Foundry registry, and the Salivaomics Knowledge Base is gone. Not a meaningful reimplementation target.

title: IntNetDB v1.0: an integrated protein-protein interaction network database generated by a probabilistic model.
data_needed: 27 heterogeneous datasets in 7 types (model-organism PPIs mapped by orthology, co-expression microarrays, domain-domain interactions, GO, phenotypes, genetic interactions, gene context), circa 2005, with HPRD (Sep 2005) as gold-standard positive and membrane/nucleus pairs as negative
where: No supplement; hanlab.genetics.ac.cn/IntNetDB.htm (gone; Wayback capture exists); HPRD (hprd.org: 503, down)
note: The 27 source datasets are cited individually (Rhodes et al. sources plus phenotype and genetic screens), but none are bundled, versioned or listed with accessions. The gold standard (HPRD Sep 2005) is unavailable because HPRD is offline. Rebuilding the integration would mean re-collecting about 27 circa-2005 datasets, several from defunct databases (BIND, early DIP, HPRD), and the result would be a different network. The predicted network itself is not deposited either.
